4.169.m: Because food serves for eating, the gift of it is supremely beneficent.

4.169.s:
prakārāṃtarabhojyāni dānānyanyāni bhārata ..
annameva paraṃ dānaṃ satyavākyaṃ paraṃ padam .. 8 ..
4.169.d:
प्रकारांतरभोज्यानि दानान्यन्यानि भारत ॥
अन्नमेव परं दानं सत्यवाक्यं परं पदम् ॥ 8 ॥
4.169.m: Other gifts are foods of different kinds, O descendant of Bharata; / food alone is the supreme gift; truthful speech is the supreme state;

4.169.s:
buddhiścārthātparo lobhaḥ santoṣaḥ paramaṃ sukham ..
snātānāmanuliptānāṃ bhūṣitānāṃ ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ .. 9 ..
4.169.d:
बुद्धिश्चार्थात्परो लोभः सन्तोषः परमं सुखम् ॥
स्नातानामनुलिप्तानां भूषितानां च भूषणैः ॥ 9 ॥
4.169.m: intelligence is higher than wealth; greed [leads to destruction], while contentment is the highest happiness. / For those who have bathed, been anointed, and are adorned with ornaments,

4.169.s:
na sukhaṃ na ca santoṣo bhavedannādṛte nṛṇām ..
śveto nāma mahīpālaḥ sārvabhaumo'bhavatpurā .. 4.169.10 ..
4.169.d:
न सुखं न च सन्तोषो भवेदन्नादृते नृणाम् ॥
श्वेतो नाम महीपालः सार्वभौमोऽभवत्पुरा ॥ 4.169.10 ॥
4.169.m:
For humans, there can be neither happiness nor satisfaction without food.
In ancient times there was an emperor named Śveta.

4.169.s:
teneṣṭaṃ bahubhiryajñaiḥ saṃgrāmā bahavo jitāḥ ..
dānāni ca pradattāni dharmataḥ pālitā mahī .. 11 ..
4.169.d:
तेनेष्टं बहुभिर्यज्ञैः संग्रामा बहवो जिताः ॥
दानानि च प्रदत्तानि धर्मतः पालिता मही ॥ 11 ॥
4.169.m:
He sacrificed with many sacrifices, won many battles,
gave gifts, and protected the earth righteously.

4.169.s:
bhuktā bhogāḥ suvipulā śatrūṇāṃ mūrdhani sthitam ..
vānaprasthena vidhinā tyaktvā rājaśriyaṃ nṛpa .. 12 ..
4.169.d:
भुक्ता भोगाः सुविपुला शत्रूणां मूर्धनि स्थितम् ॥
वानप्रस्थेन विधिना त्यक्त्वा राजश्रियं नृप ॥ 12 ॥
4.169.m:
Immense pleasures were enjoyed by him, and he stood on the heads of his enemies.
Then, renouncing royal fortune by the rule of the forest hermit, O king,

4.169.s:
svargaṃ jagāma bhuktvā tu pūjyamāno marudgaṇaiḥ ..
vimānamarkapratimaṃ pratipede mudā yutaḥ .. 13 ..
4.169.d:
स्वर्गं जगाम भुक्त्वा तु पूज्यमानो मरुद्गणैः ॥
विमानमर्कप्रतिमं प्रतिपेदे मुदा युतः ॥ 13 ॥
4.169.m:
he went to heaven after enjoying [it], worshipped by the hosts of the Maruts.
Filled with joy, he mounted a celestial chariot that was like the sun.

4.169.s:
tatrāste ramamāṇo'sau sākaṃ vidyādharaiḥ sukham ..
prasiddhaiḥ stūyate siddhaiḥ sevyate'psarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ .. 14 ..
4.169.d:
तत्रास्ते रममाणोऽसौ साकं विद्याधरैः सुखम् ॥
प्रसिद्धैः स्तूयते सिद्धैः सेव्यतेऽप्सरसां गणैः ॥ 14 ॥
4.169.m:
There he dwelt happily, rejoicing with the Vidyādharas,
praised by renowned Siddhas and served by troops of Apsarases.

4.169.s:
gaṃdharvairgīyate hṛṣṭaiḥ śakreṇāpyanugamyate ..
divyamālyāṃbaradharo divyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ .. 15 ..
4.169.d:
गंधर्वैर्गीयते हृष्टैः शक्रेणाप्यनुगम्यते ॥
दिव्यमाल्यांबरधरो दिव्याभरणभूषितः ॥ 15 ॥
4.169.m:
He was sung to by delighted Gandharvas and attended even by Śakra;
he wore celestial garlands and garments, and was adorned with celestial ornaments.

4.169.s:
sa ca nityaṃ vitānāgryādavatīrya mahītalam ..
svamāṃsānyatti kauṃteya pūrvaṃ tyaktvā kalevaram .. 16 ..
4.169.d:
स च नित्यं वितानाग्र्यादवतीर्य महीतलम् ॥
स्वमांसान्यत्ति कौंतेय पूर्वं त्यक्त्वा कलेवरम् ॥ 16 ॥
4.169.m:
And every day, descending to the surface of the earth from the best of celestial canopies,
he ate his own flesh, O son of Kuntī, having formerly abandoned his body.

4.169.s:
taccharīraṃ tathaivāste rakṣitaṃ pūrvakarmabhiḥ ..
sa kadācitsureśānaṃ brahmāṇaṃ samupasthitaḥ .. 17 ..
4.169.d:
तच्छरीरं तथैवास्ते रक्षितं पूर्वकर्मभिः ॥
स कदाचित्सुरेशानं ब्रह्माणं समुपस्थितः ॥ 17 ॥
4.169.m:
That body remained just so, preserved by his past deeds.
Once, he approached Brahmā, the lord of the gods,

4.169.s:
praṇamya prāṃjalirbhūtvā nirvedādidamabravīt ..
bhagavaṃstvatprasādena prāptaṃ svargasukhaṃ mayā .. 18 ..
4.169.d:
प्रणम्य प्रांजलिर्भूत्वा निर्वेदादिदमब्रवीत् ॥
भगवंस्त्वत्प्रसादेन प्राप्तं स्वर्गसुखं मया ॥ 18 ॥
4.169.m:
bowed down, and with cupped hands said this out of despair:
“O Lord, by your grace the happiness of heaven was attained by me,

4.169.s:
sarveṣāmapi saṃpūjyaḥ surāṇāṃ surapuṃgava ..
kiṃ tu kṣudbādhate'tyarthaṃ svargasthasyāpi me prabho .. 19 ..
4.169.d:
सर्वेषामपि संपूज्यः सुराणां सुरपुंगव ॥
किं तु क्षुद्बाधतेऽत्यर्थं स्वर्गस्थस्यापि मे प्रभो ॥ 19 ॥
4.169.m:
and I am worthy of worship even to all the gods, O bull among gods.
Yet hunger torments me exceedingly, O Lord, even though I abide in heaven,

4.169.s:
yayā māṃsānyahaṃ svasya bhakṣyayāmyaśanaṃ vinā ..
.. brahmovāca .. ..
śvetābhijanasaṃpanna śveta śṛṇu vaco mama .. 4.169.20 ..
4.169.d:
यया मांसान्यहं स्वस्य भक्ष्ययाम्यशनं विना ॥
॥ ब्रह्मोवाच ॥ ॥
श्वेताभिजनसंपन्न श्वेत शृणु वचो मम ॥ 4.169.20 ॥
4.169.m:
because of which I consume my own flesh, being without food.”
Brahmā said:
“O Śveta, born of noble lineage, listen to my words.

4.169.s:
tvayādhītaṃ hutaṃ dattaṃ guravaḥ paritoṣitāḥ ..
nāśanaṃ bhavatā dattaṃ yaddvijebhyo narādhipa .. 21 ..
4.169.d:
त्वयाधीतं हुतं दत्तं गुरवः परितोषिताः ॥
नाशनं भवता दत्तं यद्द्विजेभ्यो नराधिप ॥ 21 ॥
4.169.m:
You studied [the Vedas], made oblations, gave gifts, and satisfied your preceptors.
Yet no food was given by you to the twice-born, O lord of men.

4.169.s:
anannadānasya phalaṃ tvayedamupabhujyate ..
tarhyannadānato nānyaccharīrārogyakārakam .. .. 22 ..
4.169.d:
अनन्नदानस्य फलं त्वयेदमुपभुज्यते ॥
तर्ह्यन्नदानतो नान्यच्छरीरारोग्यकारकम् ॥ ॥ 22 ॥
4.169.m:
This fruit of not giving food is now being experienced by you.
Therefore, nothing other than the gift of food produces health for the body;

4.169.s:
nānyadannādṛte puṃsāṃ kiñcitsañjīvanauṣadham ..
mahīṃ gatvā mahārāja kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama .. 23 ..
4.169.d:
नान्यदन्नादृते पुंसां किञ्चित्सञ्जीवनौषधम् ॥
महीं गत्वा महाराज कुरुष्व वचनं मम ॥ 23 ॥
4.169.m:
for men there is no other medicine that restores life except food.
Go to the earth, O great king, and carry out my word:

4.169.s:
tapaḥ svādhyāyasaṃpanne śāstrajñe saṃjitendriye ..
yena saṃpadyate tṛptirakṣayā kṣmāṃpate tava .. 24 ..
4.169.d:
तपः स्वाध्यायसंपन्ने शास्त्रज्ञे संजितेन्द्रिये ॥
येन संपद्यते तृप्तिरक्षया क्ष्मांपते तव ॥ 24 ॥
4.169.m:
[give food] to one rich in austerity and Vedic study, knowledgeable in the śāstras, and of conquered senses,
by which imperishable satisfaction will be accomplished for you, O lord of the earth.”

4.169.s:
viriṃcervacanādgatvā tvarāyukto mahītalam ..
agastyaṃ bhojayāmāsa bhaktyā bharatasattama .. .. 25 ..
4.169.d:
विरिंचेर्वचनाद्गत्वा त्वरायुक्तो महीतलम् ॥
अगस्त्यं भोजयामास भक्त्या भरतसत्तम ॥ ॥ 25 ॥
4.169.m:
Having gone with haste to the surface of the earth on the command of Viriñci,
he fed Agastya with devotion, O best of the Bharatas.

4.169.s:
bhojayitvā tataḥ prādāddakṣiṇāṃ kṣīṇakalmaṣaḥ ..
ekāvaliṃ svakātkaṇṭhātsamuttārya samujjvalām .. 26 ..
4.169.d:
भोजयित्वा ततः प्रादाद्दक्षिणां क्षीणकल्मषः ॥
एकावलिं स्वकात्कण्ठात्समुत्तार्य समुज्ज्वलाम् ॥ 26 ॥
4.169.m:
Having fed him, his sins dispelled, he then gave as a priestly gift
a radiant single-stringed pearl necklace, taking it off from his own neck.

4.169.s:
tato dundubhighoṣeṇa pūjitaḥ surasattamaiḥ ..
śvetastṛpto gataḥ svargaṃ dattvānnaṃ dakṣiṇāyutam .. 27 ..
4.169.d:
ततो दुन्दुभिघोषेण पूजितः सुरसत्तमैः ॥
श्वेतस्तृप्तो गतः स्वर्गं दत्त्वान्नं दक्षिणायुतम् ॥ 27 ॥
4.169.m:
Then, worshipped by the best of the gods with the roll of war drums,
Śveta, now satisfied, went to heaven after giving food along with a priestly gift.

4.169.s:
paulastye nihate paścāddevadānavasaṃkaṭe ..
rāmāyaikāvaliṃ prādādagastyaḥ parayā mudā .. 28 ..
4.169.d:
पौलस्त्ये निहते पश्चाद्देवदानवसंकटे ॥
रामायैकावलिं प्रादादगस्त्यः परया मुदा ॥ 28 ॥
4.169.m:
Later, when Rāvaṇa was slain in the crisis between gods and Dānavas,
Agastya gave that single-stringed necklace to Rāma with supreme joy.

4.169.s:
etadannasya māhātmyaṃ kathayāmyaparaṃ ca te ..
na cānnādaparaṃ kiñcitsatyaṃ tava mayoditam .. 29 ..
4.169.d:
एतदन्नस्य माहात्म्यं कथयाम्यपरं च ते ॥
न चान्नादपरं किञ्चित्सत्यं तव मयोदितम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.169.m:
This is the greatness of food; I shall tell you more.
And there is nothing beyond food; the truth has been spoken to you by me.

4.169.s:
annaṃ vai prāṇināṃ prāṇā annamojo balaṃ sukham ..
etasmātkāraṇātsadbhirannadaḥ prāṇadaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 4.169.30 ..
4.169.d:
अन्नं वै प्राणिनां प्राणा अन्नमोजो बलं सुखम् ॥
एतस्मात्कारणात्सद्भिरन्नदः प्राणदः स्मृतः ॥ 4.169.30 ॥
4.169.m:
Food is indeed the breath of life of living beings; food is vitality, strength, and happiness.
For this reason, the giver of food is regarded by the good as the giver of life.

4.169.s:
sudūrādāśayā yasya gṛhaṃ prāptā bubhukṣitāḥ ..
tṛptāḥ pratinivartaṃte ko'nyastatsadṛśaḥ pumān ..31..
4.169.d:
सुदूरादाशया यस्य गृहं प्राप्ता बुभुक्षिताः ॥
तृप्ताः प्रतिनिवर्तंते कोऽन्यस्तत्सदृशः पुमान् ॥31॥
4.169.m:
Who else is equal to that man, to whose house the hungry come
from afar with hope, and return satisfied?

4.169.s:
dīkṣitaḥ kapilā satrī rājā bhikṣurmahodadhiḥ ..
dṛṣṭamātrā punaṃtyete tasmātpaśyaṃti nityaśaḥ .. 32 ..
4.169.d:
दीक्षितः कपिला सत्री राजा भिक्षुर्महोदधिः ॥
दृष्टमात्रा पुनंत्येते तस्मात्पश्यंति नित्यशः ॥ 32 ॥
4.169.m:
An initiated person, a brown cow, an uninterrupted sacrificer, a king, a mendicant, and the great ocean—
these purify as soon as they are seen; therefore one should see them constantly.

4.169.s:
ekasyāpyatitherannaṃ yaḥ pradātumaśaktimān..
tasyā''rambhaiḥ parikleśairvasataḥ kiṃ phalaṃ gṛhe .. 33 ..
4.169.d:
एकस्याप्यतिथेरन्नं यः प्रदातुमशक्तिमान्॥
तस्या'ऽरम्भैः परिक्लेशैर्वसतः किं फलं गृहे ॥ 33 ॥
4.169.m:
One who is unable to give food even to a single guest—
what is the fruit of his dwelling in a house with undertakings and troubles?

4.169.s:
śakyate duṣkare'pyarthe cirarātrāya jīvitum ..
na tvāhāravihīnena śakyaṃ vartayituṃ ciram .. 34 ..
4.169.d:
शक्यते दुष्करेऽप्यर्थे चिररात्राय जीवितुम् ॥
न त्वाहारविहीनेन शक्यं वर्तयितुं चिरम् ॥ 34 ॥
4.169.m:
It is possible to live for a long time even in difficult circumstances,
but it is not possible to endure long without nourishment.

4.169.s:
bhuktvā gṛhe gṛhasthasya maithunaṃ yaśca sevate ..
yasyānnaṃ tasya te putrā iti prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ .. 35 ..
4.169.d:
भुक्त्वा गृहे गृहस्थस्य मैथुनं यश्च सेवते ॥
यस्यान्नं तस्य ते पुत्रा इति प्राहुर्मनीषिणः ॥ 35 ॥
4.169.m:
And he who engages in sexual intercourse after eating in the house of a householder—
those sons belong to the one whose food it is: so say the wise.

4.169.s:
duṣkṛtaṃ hi manuṣyāṇāmannamāśritya tiṣṭhati ..
yo yasyānnaṃ samaśnāti sa tasyāśnāti duṣkṛtam .. 36 ..
4.169.d:
दुष्कृतं हि मनुष्याणामन्नमाश्रित्य तिष्ठति ॥
यो यस्यान्नं समश्नाति स तस्याश्नाति दुष्कृतम् ॥ 36 ॥
4.169.m:
For the misdeed of human beings resides based upon food;
he who eats someone's food eats his misdeed.

4.169.s:
vanaspatigate some parānnaṃ yastu bhuṃjati ..
tasya māsakṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ dātāramupagacchati .. 37 ..
4.169.d:
वनस्पतिगते सोमे परान्नं यस्तु भुंजति ॥
तस्य मासकृतं पुण्यं दातारमुपगच्छति ॥ 37 ॥
4.169.m:
He who eats the food of another when the moon has entered the vegetation [at the new moon],
the religious merit made by him over a month goes to the giver.

4.169.s:
kasmānna dīyate nityaṃ kasmādannaṃ na dīyate ..
yasyedṛśī phalāvāptiḥ kathitā pūrvasūribhiḥ .. 38 ..
4.169.d:
कस्मान्न दीयते नित्यं कस्मादन्नं न दीयते ॥
यस्येदृशी फलावाप्तिः कथिता पूर्वसूरिभिः ॥ 38 ॥
4.169.m:
Why is it not given constantly? Why is food not given,
whose attainment of fruit is told thus by ancient sages?

4.169.s:
bhikṣāṃ vā puṣkalāṃ vāpi haṃtakāraṃ dvijātaye ..
bhojanaṃ vā yathālābhamadattvāśnāti kilbiṣam .. 39 ..
4.169.d:
भिक्षां वा पुष्कलां वापि हंतकारं द्विजातये ॥
भोजनं वा यथालाभमदत्त्वाश्नाति किल्बिषम् ॥ 39 ॥
4.169.m:
Without giving an alms-portion, or a generous portion, or an offering to the twice-born,
or food according to what is available, one eats sin.

4.169.s:
yenāyutaṃ sahasraṃ vā bhojitaṃ syāddvijanmanām ..
tena brahmagṛhāsannaṃ nūnaṃ baddhaṃ kuṭīrakam .. 4.169.40 ..
4.169.d:
येनायुतं सहस्रं वा भोजितं स्याद्द्विजन्मनाम् ॥
तेन ब्रह्मगृहासन्नं नूनं बद्धं कुटीरकम् ॥ 4.169.40 ॥
4.169.m:
By him by whom ten thousand or a thousand twice-born have been fed,
a small cottage has surely been built near the abode of Brahmā.

4.169.s:
vārāṇasyāṃ purā pārtha vaṇigāpaṇajīvanaḥ ..
dhaneśvara iti khyāto devabrāhmaṇapūjakaḥ.. 41 ..
4.169.d:
वाराणस्यां पुरा पार्थ वणिगापणजीवनः ॥
धनेश्वर इति ख्यातो देवब्राह्मणपूजकः॥ 41 ॥
4.169.m:
Formerly in Vārāṇasī, O son of Pṛthā, there was a merchant who lived by shopkeeping,
renowned as Dhaneśvara, who worshipped gods and brāhmaṇas.

4.169.s:
tasyāpaṇaikadeśe tu muktvāṃḍaṃ pāṃḍuracchavi ..
sasarpa sarpastaddeśādvaṇigdṛṣṭvā viśaṃkitaḥ .. 42 ..
4.169.d:
तस्यापणैकदेशे तु मुक्त्वांडं पांडुरच्छवि ॥
ससर्प सर्पस्तद्देशाद्वणिग्दृष्ट्वा विशंकितः ॥ 42 ॥
4.169.m:
In one part of his shop, after depositing a pale-hued egg,
a snake slithered away from that place; seeing it, the merchant became apprehensive.

4.169.s:
tadaṃḍaṃ vaṇijā tena dṛṣṭaṃ kāruṇyabuddhinā ..
tataḥ prabhṛtyanudinaṃ rarakṣa ca puṣoṣa ca .. 43 ..
4.169.d:
तदंडं वणिजा तेन दृष्टं कारुण्यबुद्धिना ॥
ततः प्रभृत्यनुदिनं ररक्ष च पुषोष च ॥ 43 ॥
4.169.m:
That egg was seen by that merchant with a mind of compassion;
from that time on, he protected and nourished it day after day.

4.169.s:
nirjagāma dinaiḥ kaiścidbhitvāṃḍaṃ sarpapotakaḥ ..
taṃ vaṇikkṣīrapānādyairupacārairavardhayat .. 44 ..
4.169.d:
निर्जगाम दिनैः कैश्चिद्भित्वांडं सर्पपोतकः ॥
तं वणिक्क्षीरपानाद्यैरुपचारैरवर्धयत् ॥ 44 ॥
4.169.m:
After some days, a young snake emerged, breaking the egg;
the merchant reared it with care, giving it milk to drink and the like.

4.169.s:
lilihe ghṛtabhāṃḍāni jighre ca gaṃdhasaṃcayān ..
luloṭha pāṃsuprakare cacāra vārimadhyagaḥ .. 45 ..
4.169.d:
लिलिहे घृतभांडानि जिघ्रे च गंधसंचयान् ॥
लुलोठ पांसुप्रकरे चचार वारिमध्यगः ॥ 45 ॥
4.169.m:
It licked the jars of clarified butter, smelled the heaps of perfumes,
rolled in the dust heap, and moved about in the water.

4.169.s:
vaṇijā rakṣyamāṇaḥ sa snehāccāharahaḥ punaḥ ..
jagāma sumahānkālo'bhavadeṣa bhayaṃkaraḥ .. 46 ..
4.169.d:
वणिजा रक्ष्यमाणः स स्नेहाच्चाहरहः पुनः ॥
जगाम सुमहान्कालोऽभवदेष भयंकरः ॥ 46 ॥
4.169.m:
Being protected by the merchant with affection day after day,
a great deal of time passed, and it grew terrifying.

4.169.s:
athaikasmindine gaṃgāṃ gataḥ snātuṃ trilokagām ..
vaṇigāpaṇe paṇyavidaṃ sthāpayitvā sutaṃ matam .. 47 ..
4.169.d:
अथैकस्मिन्दिने गंगां गतः स्नातुं त्रिलोकगाम् ॥
वणिगापणे पण्यविदं स्थापयित्वा सुतं मतम् ॥ 47 ॥
4.169.m:
Then, one day, having placed his esteemed son who was knowledgeable in goods in the shop,
the merchant went to the Gaṅgā, which traverses the three worlds, to bathe.

4.169.s:
vyavahartuṃ samārabdhaṃ vaṇikputreṇa dhīmatā ..
dadāti pratigṛhṇāti ghṛtatailayavaikṣavam.. 48 ..
4.169.d:
व्यवहर्तुं समारब्धं वणिक्पुत्रेण धीमता ॥
ददाति प्रतिगृह्णाति घृततैलयवैक्षवम्॥ 48 ॥
4.169.m:
Business was begun by the wise merchant's son:
he gave and received clarified butter, oil, barley, and sugarcane.

4.169.s:
vyavahārākulatayā pādayoraṃtareṇa saḥ ..
sarpaścacāla cāpalyādvaṇigvikṣepamabhyagāt .. 49 ..
4.169.d:
व्यवहाराकुलतया पादयोरंतरेण सः ॥
सर्पश्चचाल चापल्याद्वणिग्विक्षेपमभ्यगात् ॥ 49 ॥
4.169.m:
Owing to the bustle of transactions, that snake moved between his feet
out of restlessness, and reached the merchant's side.

4.169.s:
jānannapi tadvṛttāṃtaṃ nidāne niyatervaśāt ..
trāsātsaṃtarjayāmāsa balena padacāriṇam .. .. 4.169.50 ..
4.169.d:
जानन्नपि तद्वृत्तांतं निदाने नियतेर्वशात् ॥
त्रासात्संतर्जयामास बलेन पदचारिणम् ॥ ॥ 4.169.50 ॥
4.169.m:
Though knowing its history, yet compelled by fate at that critical moment,
out of terror he violently threatened the creature moving on foot.

4.169.s:
sa mahītaḥ samutthāya mūrddhānamavaruhya ca ..
uvāca dāruṇataraṃ vacanaṃ pannagādhamaḥ .. 51 ..
4.169.d:
स महीतः समुत्थाय मूर्द्धानमवरुह्य च ॥
उवाच दारुणतरं वचनं पन्नगाधमः ॥ 51 ॥
4.169.m:
Rising from the ground and lowering its hood,
that vile serpent uttered most dreadful words:

4.169.s:
śaraṇāgataṃ poṣitaṃ ca tava pitrā priyaṃkaram ..
kasmānmāṃ haṃsi duṣṭātmankathaṃ jīvanvimokṣyase .. 52 ..
4.169.d:
शरणागतं पोषितं च तव पित्रा प्रियंकरम् ॥
कस्मान्मां हंसि दुष्टात्मन्कथं जीवन्विमोक्ष्यसे ॥ 52 ॥
4.169.m:
“I came for refuge, was nourished by your father, and did what was pleasing;
why do you strike me, evil-minded one? How will you escape alive?”

4.169.s:
anaṃtaraṃ kalakalaḥ saṃjāto rodatāṃ nṛṇām ..
dhaneśvarasuto daṣṭaḥ sarpeṇāpi bhṛśākulaḥ .. .. 53 ..
4.169.d:
अनंतरं कलकलः संजातो रोदतां नृणाम् ॥
धनेश्वरसुतो दष्टः सर्पेणापि भृशाकुलः ॥ ॥ 53 ॥
4.169.m:
Immediately a tumult arose among the weeping people;
and Dhaneśvara’s son, bitten by the snake, became exceedingly distressed.

4.169.s:
acyutānaṃta goviṃda kṛṣṇakṛṣṇetyudīrayan..
dhaneśvaropyanuprāptaḥ provācākulayā girā .. 54 ..
4.169.d:
अच्युतानंत गोविंद कृष्णकृष्णेत्युदीरयन्॥
धनेश्वरोप्यनुप्राप्तः प्रोवाचाकुलया गिरा ॥ 54 ॥
4.169.m: Uttering, "Acyuta, Ananta, Govinda, Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa!", / Dhaneśvara also arrived and spoke with an agitated voice:

4.169.s:
kiṃ kṛtaṃ mama putreṇa tava pavraga vipriyam ..
yadayaṃ bhavatā mūrdhni svabhogenābhiveṣṭitaḥ .. 55 ..
4.169.d:
किं कृतं मम पुत्रेण तव पव्रग विप्रियम् ॥
यदयं भवता मूर्ध्नि स्वभोगेनाभिवेष्टितः ॥ 55 ॥
4.169.m: "What unpleasant thing was done to you, O serpent, by my son, / that he has been wrapped around his head by your coil?

4.169.s:
mūrkha mitraṃ susaṃbaṃdhaṃ hīnajātijano hi yaḥ ..
yaḥ karotyabuthoṃgārānsa svahastena karṣati .. .. 56 ..
4.169.d:
मूर्ख मित्रं सुसंबंधं हीनजातिजनो हि यः ॥
यः करोत्यबुथोंगारान्स स्वहस्तेन कर्षति ॥ ॥ 56 ॥
4.169.m: For whoever makes a fool, a low-born person, a friend or a close associate, / he who does so unwisely drags hot coals with his own hand."

4.169.s:
tamuvāca ca sarpo'sau vāṣpagadgadayā girā ..
niraparādho bhavataḥ putreṇāhaṃ samāhataḥ .. 57 ..
4.169.d:
तमुवाच च सर्पोऽसौ वाष्पगद्गदया गिरा ॥
निरपराधो भवतः पुत्रेणाहं समाहतः ॥ 57 ॥
4.169.m: And that serpent said to him with a voice choked with tears: / "I, guiltless, was struck by your son.

4.169.s:
tadahaṃ paśyataste'dya daśāmyenaṃ narādhipa ..
yathā na bhūyo bhūtānāṃ bhavedasmātkvacidbhayam .. 58 ..
4.169.d:
तदहं पश्यतस्तेऽद्य दशाम्येनं नराधिप ॥
यथा न भूयो भूतानां भवेदस्मात्क्वचिद्भयम् ॥ 58 ॥
4.169.m: Therefore, right before your eyes, O lord of men, I will bite him today, / so that there will never again be fear of him for any living beings."

4.169.s:
.. dhaneśvara uvāca .. ..
upakāraṃ vrataṃ bhaktyā snehapāro na yasya ca ..
satāṃ mārgamapākramya prayātaḥ kena vāryate .. 59 ..
4.169.d:
॥ धनेश्वर उवाच ॥ ॥
उपकारं व्रतं भक्त्या स्नेहपारो न यस्य च ॥
सतां मार्गमपाक्रम्य प्रयातः केन वार्यते ॥ 59 ॥
4.169.m: Dhaneśvara said: / "He who has no devotion for the practice of doing good, nor limit to affection, / departing from the path of the virtuous, by whom can he be stopped?

4.169.s:
kṣaṇamātraṃ pratīkṣasva yāvadeva śiśurmama ..
aurdhvadehikakarmāṇi karoti svayamātmanaḥ .. 4.169.60 ..
4.169.d:
क्षणमात्रं प्रतीक्षस्व यावदेव शिशुर्मम ॥
और्ध्वदेहिककर्माणि करोति स्वयमात्मनः ॥ 4.169.60 ॥
4.169.m: Wait for just a moment, so that my child / may perform his own funeral rites himself."

4.169.s:
evamuktā gṛhaṃ gatvā yatīnāṃ brahmacāriṇām ..
sahasraṃ bhojayāmāsa ghṛtapāyasabhojanaiḥ ..61 ..
4.169.d:
एवमुक्ता गृहं गत्वा यतीनां ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ॥
सहस्रं भोजयामास घृतपायसभोजनैः ॥61 ॥
4.169.m: Having spoken thus and gone home, he fed a thousand / ascetics and celibate students with meals of ghee and milk-rice.

4.169.s:
samutthāya tataḥ sarve brāhmaṇā hṛṣṭamānasāḥ ..
vaṇikputrasyottamāṃge cikṣipuḥ kusumākṣatān .. 62 ..
4.169.d:
समुत्थाय ततः सर्वे ब्राह्मणा हृष्टमानसाः ॥
वणिक्पुत्रस्योत्तमांगे चिक्षिपुः कुसुमाक्षतान् ॥ 62 ॥
4.169.m: Then, rising up, all the brāhmaṇas with joyful hearts / scattered flowers and unbroken grains of rice upon the merchant's son's head:

4.169.s:
vaṇikputra ciraṃ jīva naśyaṃtu tava śatravaḥ ..
abhīṣṭaphalasaṃsiddhirastu te brāhmaṇājñayā .. 63 ..
4.169.d:
वणिक्पुत्र चिरं जीव नश्यंतु तव शत्रवः ॥
अभीष्टफलसंसिद्धिरस्तु ते ब्राह्मणाज्ञया ॥ 63 ॥
4.169.m: "O merchant's son, live long! May your enemies perish! / May the attainment of your desired result come to pass by the command of the brāhmaṇas!"

4.169.s:
tataḥ sa duṣṭaprakṛtirvipra vāgvajratāḍitaḥ ..
pannago nagasaṃkāśaḥ papāta ca mamāra ca .. 64 ..
4.169.d:
ततः स दुष्टप्रकृतिर्विप्र वाग्वज्रताडितः ॥
पन्नगो नगसंकाशः पपात च ममार च ॥ 64 ॥
4.169.m: Then that wicked-natured serpent, struck by the thunderbolt of the brāhmaṇas' words, / looking like a mountain, fell down and died.

4.169.s:
vipannaṃ pannagaṃ dṛṣṭvā trastacakṣurdhaneśvaraḥ ..
āḥ kimetaditi procya viṣādamagamatparam .. 65 ..
4.169.d:
विपन्नं पन्नगं दृष्ट्वा त्रस्तचक्षुर्धनेश्वरः ॥
आः किमेतदिति प्रोच्य विषादमगमत्परम् ॥ 65 ॥
4.169.m: Seeing the serpent perished, Dhaneśvara, with frightened eyes, / exclaimed, "Ah, what is this!" and fell into extreme dejection:

4.169.s:
poṣito'yaṃ mayā bālaḥ pālito lālitastathā ..
mamāpacārātpaṃcatvamāpannaḥ pavanāśanaḥ .. 66 ..
4.169.d:
पोषितोऽयं मया बालः पालितो लालितस्तथा ॥
ममापचारात्पंचत्वमापन्नः पवनाशनः ॥ 66 ॥
4.169.m: "This boy was nourished by me, protected and fondled; / yet because of my fault, the air-eater has met with death.

4.169.s:
upakāriṣu yaḥ sādhuḥ sādhutve tasya ko guṇaḥ ..
apakāriṣu yaḥ sādhuḥ sa sādhuḥ sadbhiriṣyate .. 67 ..
4.169.d:
उपकारिषु यः साधुः साधुत्वे तस्य को गुणः ॥
अपकारिषु यः साधुः स साधुः सद्भिरिष्यते ॥ 67 ॥
4.169.m: He who is good to those who do good, what merit is there in his goodness? / He who is good to those who do harm, he is regarded as good by the virtuous."

4.169.s:
ityevamavadhāryāsau duḥkhasaṃtaptamānasaḥ ..
bubhuje nākulatayā na ca suṣvāpa tāṃ niśām .. 68 ..
4.169.d:
इत्येवमवधार्यासौ दुःखसंतप्तमानसः ॥
बुभुजे नाकुलतया न च सुष्वाप तां निशाम् ॥ 68 ॥
4.169.m: Reflecting thus, his mind tormented by sorrow, / in his agitation he did not eat, nor did he sleep that night.

4.169.s:
tataḥ prabhāte gaṃgāyāṃ snātvā saṃtarpya devatāḥ ..
sahasraṃ bhojayāmāsa punareva dvijanmanām .. 69 ..
4.169.d:
ततः प्रभाते गंगायां स्नात्वा संतर्प्य देवताः ॥
सहस्रं भोजयामास पुनरेव द्विजन्मनाम् ॥ 69 ॥
4.169.m: Then in the morning, having bathed in the Gaṅgā and gratified the deities, / he once again fed a thousand of the twice-born.

4.169.s:
tairbhuktairiṣṭasaṃsiddhairbrāhmaṇai ranumoditaḥ..
vaṇikprāha mamābhīṣṭaṃ saṃjīvatveṣa pannagaḥ .. 4.169.70 ..
4.169.d:
तैर्भुक्तैरिष्टसंसिद्धैर्ब्राह्मणै रनुमोदितः॥
वणिक्प्राह ममाभीष्टं संजीवत्वेष पन्नगः ॥ 4.169.70 ॥
4.169.m: Approved by those brāhmaṇas, who had eaten and attained their desired satisfaction, / the merchant said: "My wish is that this serpent may be revived!"

4.169.s:
tato dvijavaronmuktairaṃbubhiḥ pariṣiṃcitaḥ ..
udatiṣṭhadahīnāṃgaḥ sahasā hi mahākulaḥ .. .. 71 ..
4.169.d:
ततो द्विजवरोन्मुक्तैरंबुभिः परिषिंचितः ॥
उदतिष्ठदहीनांगः सहसा हि महाकुलः ॥ ॥ 71 ॥
4.169.m: Then, sprinkled with waters released by the excellent twice-born, / of complete limbs and of noble breed, it suddenly stood up.

4.169.s:
praharṣamatulaṃ lebhe dṛṣṭvā taṃ purataḥ sthitam ..
pratyagrāvayavaṃ dṛṣṭvā sṛkkiṇīparileliham .. 72 ..
4.169.d:
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे दृष्ट्वा तं पुरतः स्थितम् ॥
प्रत्यग्रावयवं दृष्ट्वा सृक्किणीपरिलेलिहम् ॥ 72 ॥
4.169.m: He experienced peerless joy seeing it standing before him, / seeing its limbs renewed, repeatedly licking the corners of its mouth.

4.169.s:
sādhuvādo mahāñjātaḥ praśaśaṃsurdhaneśvaram ..
purīnivāsinaḥ sarve vismayotphullalocanāḥ ..73..
4.169.d:
साधुवादो महाञ्जातः प्रशशंसुर्धनेश्वरम् ॥
पुरीनिवासिनः सर्वे विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनाः ॥73॥
4.169.m: A great cry of "Well done!" arose; all the city dwellers, / their eyes wide with wonder, praised Dhaneśvara.

4.169.s:
sahasrabhojyamāhātmyaṃ kathitaṃ te yudhiṣṭhira ..
samyakchraddhāprayuktasya kimanyatkathayāmi te ..75..
4.169.d:
सहस्रभोज्यमाहात्म्यं कथितं ते युधिष्ठिर ॥
सम्यक्छ्रद्धाप्रयुक्तस्य किमन्यत्कथयामि ते ॥75॥
4.169.m: The greatness of feeding a thousand has been narrated to you, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / who are endowed with perfect faith; what else shall I tell you?

4.169.s:
yacchaṃti ye'nudivasaṃ dvijapuṃgavānāmannaṃ viśuddhamanaso bhṛśamāgatānām ..
martye vihṛtya suciraṃ sasuhṛjjanāste pretya prayāṃti bhavanaṃ muditā murāreḥ..77..
sthālīdānavarṇanam
4.169.d:
यच्छंति येऽनुदिवसं द्विजपुंगवानामन्नं विशुद्धमनसो भृशमागतानाम् ॥
मर्त्ये विहृत्य सुचिरं ससुहृज्जनास्ते प्रेत्य प्रयांति भवनं मुदिता मुरारेः॥77॥
स्थालीदानवर्णनम्
4.169.m:
Those who, with a purified mind, daily offer food to the best of the twice-born who have arrived, / having enjoyed themselves for a long time among mortals together with their kin, go upon dying, full of joy, to the abode of Murāri.
Description of the Gift of a Cooking Pot

4.170.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
annadānaprasaṃgena mamāpi smṛtimāgatam ..
tatte'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi śrutaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ ca yanmayā .. 1 ..
4.170.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
अन्नदानप्रसंगेन ममापि स्मृतिमागतम् ॥
तत्तेऽहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि श्रुतं दृष्टं च यन्मया ॥ 1 ॥
4.170.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / "In connection with the gift of food, a memory has come to me as well; / that which was heard and seen by me, I will tell you.

4.170.s:
akṣadyūtena bhagavandhanaṃ rājyaṃ ca no hṛtam ..
āhūya niṣkṛtiprājñaiḥ kitavairakṣakovidaiḥ ..2..
4.170.d:
अक्षद्यूतेन भगवन्धनं राज्यं च नो हृतम् ॥
आहूय निष्कृतिप्राज्ञैः कितवैरक्षकोविदैः ॥2॥
4.170.m: O Blessed One, in a game of dice our wealth and kingdom were stolen, / when we were summoned by rogues skilled in dice and clever in trickery.

4.170.s:
vanaṃ prasthāpitāḥ sarve valkalājinavāsasaḥ ..
draupadyā sahitāḥ kṛṣṇa karṇaduryo dhanādibhiḥ .. 3 ..
4.170.d:
वनं प्रस्थापिताः सर्वे वल्कलाजिनवाससः ॥
द्रौपद्या सहिताः कृष्ण कर्णदुर्यो धनादिभिः ॥ 3 ॥
4.170.m: We were all dispatched to the forest wearing bark and animal skins, / along with Draupadī, O Kṛṣṇa, by Karṇa, Duryodhana, and the others.

4.170.s:
jñātvā vanagatānasmānbrāhmaṇāḥ saṃjiteṃdriyāḥ ..
draṣṭumabhyāyayuḥ sarve paurāścāpyanujagmire .. 4 ..
4.170.d:
ज्ञात्वा वनगतानस्मान्ब्राह्मणाः संजितेंद्रियाः ॥
द्रष्टुमभ्याययुः सर्वे पौराश्चाप्यनुजग्मिरे ॥ 4 ॥
4.170.m: Knowing that we had gone to the forest, brāhmaṇas with subdued senses / all came to see us, and the citizens followed as well.

4.170.s:
asmānsnehātkliśyamānā dṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇasattamāḥ ..
paurānkarmakarāṃścaiva nirvedādidamabruvan .. 5 ..
4.170.d:
अस्मान्स्नेहात्क्लिश्यमाना दृष्ट्वा ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः ॥
पौरान्कर्मकरांश्चैव निर्वेदादिदमब्रुवन् ॥ 5 ॥
4.170.m: Seeing us suffering out of affection, those best of brāhmaṇas, / along with the citizens and servants, spoke this out of despondency:

4.170.s:
jīvato yasya jīvaṃti viprā mitrāṇi bāṃdhavāḥ ..
jīvanaṃ tasya saphalamātmārthe ko na jīvati .. 6 ..
4.170.d:
जीवतो यस्य जीवंति विप्रा मित्राणि बांधवाः ॥
जीवनं तस्य सफलमात्मार्थे को न जीवति ॥ 6 ॥
4.170.m: "He during whose life the vipras, friends, and kinsmen live, / his life is fruitful; who does not live for his own sake?

4.170.s:
abhyāgataṃ suhṛdvargaṃ kuṭuṃbamapahāya ca ..
jīvannapi mṛtaḥ pāpaḥ kevalaṃ svodaraṃbhariḥ .. 7 ..
4.170.d:
अभ्यागतं सुहृद्वर्गं कुटुंबमपहाय च ॥
जीवन्नपि मृतः पापः केवलं स्वोदरंभरिः ॥ 7 ॥
4.170.m: Abandoning the arrived guest, the circle of friends, and the family, / living only to fill his own belly, a wicked man is dead even while alive."

4.170.s:
ityevamavadhāryāhaṃ tānṛṣīnpunarabruvam ..
bhavaṃtaḥ sarva evātra trikālajñā maharṣayaḥ .. 8 ..
4.170.d:
इत्येवमवधार्याहं तानृषीन्पुनरब्रुवम् ॥
भवंतः सर्व एवात्र त्रिकालज्ञा महर्षयः ॥ 8 ॥
4.170.m: Reflecting thus, I spoke once more to those sages: / "All of you present here are great sages knowing the three times,

4.170.s:
samāgatā matpriyārthaṃ jñānavijñānapāragāḥ ..
brūta kaṃcidupāyaṃ me bhavaṃtobhijanaṃ prati .. .. 9 ..
4.170.d:
समागता मत्प्रियार्थं ज्ञानविज्ञानपारगाः ॥
ब्रूत कंचिदुपायं मे भवंतोभिजनं प्रति ॥ ॥ 9 ॥
4.170.m: gathered for my sake, masters of knowledge and discernment. / Tell me some means with regard to these relatives,

4.170.s:
bhavadbhiḥ sahitāḥ sarve bhṛtyairbhrātṛbhireva ca ..
nirgaccheyaṃ vane śūnye dvādaśemāḥ samā yathā ..4.170.1 0..
4.170.d:
भवद्भिः सहिताः सर्वे भृत्यैर्भ्रातृभिरेव च ॥
निर्गच्छेयं वने शून्ये द्वादशेमाः समा यथा ॥4.170.1 0॥
4.170.m: so that accompanied by you all, along with servants and brothers, / I may pass these twelve years in the empty forest."

4.170.s:
māmuvācātha maitreyaḥ śṛṇu kauṃteya madvacaḥ ..
pūrvavṛttaṃ pravakṣyāmi dṛṣṭaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā .. 11 ..
4.170.d:
मामुवाचाथ मैत्रेयः शृणु कौंतेय मद्वचः ॥
पूर्ववृत्तं प्रवक्ष्यामि दृष्टं दिव्येन चक्षुषा ॥ 11 ॥
4.170.m: Then Maitreya said to me: "Listen, O son of Kuntī, to my words. / I will tell of an event of the past, seen with divine vision.

4.170.s:
āsīttapovane kācidbrāhmaṇī brahmacāriṇī ..
durbhagā durgatā duḥkhādārādhayati sā dvijān .. .. 12 ..
4.170.d:
आसीत्तपोवने काचिद्ब्राह्मणी ब्रह्मचारिणी ॥
दुर्भगा दुर्गता दुःखादाराधयति सा द्विजान् ॥ ॥ 12 ॥
4.170.m: In a penance grove there was a certain brāhmaṇa woman observing celibacy, / unfortunate and destitute; out of distress she served the twice-born.

4.170.s:
śaucena tuṣṭā munayaḥ praśrayeṇa damena ca ..
procurvada viśālākṣi kiṃ kurmastava suvrate .. 13 ..
4.170.d:
शौचेन तुष्टा मुनयः प्रश्रयेण दमेन च ॥
प्रोचुर्वद विशालाक्षि किं कुर्मस्तव सुव्रते ॥ 13 ॥
4.170.m: Pleased with her purity, humility, and self-restraint, the sages / said: 'Speak, O large-eyed woman, what shall we do for you, O woman of good vows?'

4.170.s:
sā tānuvāca kiṃ tanme vrataṃ dānamathāpi vā ..
kathayadhvaṃ bhaveyaṃ vai yena śrīsukhabhāginī .. 14 ..
4.170.d:
सा तानुवाच किं तन्मे व्रतं दानमथापि वा ॥
कथयध्वं भवेयं वै येन श्रीसुखभागिनी ॥ 14 ॥
4.170.m: She said to them: 'What is that votive observance or gift for me? / Tell me that by which I may truly become a sharer in prosperity and happiness,

4.170.s:
ādhārabhūtā bhūtānāṃ bahvapatyā patipriyā ..
spṛhaṇīyā trijagatāṃ trivargaphalabhāginī .. .. 15 ..
4.170.d:
आधारभूता भूतानां बह्वपत्या पतिप्रिया ॥
स्पृहणीया त्रिजगतां त्रिवर्गफलभागिनी ॥ ॥ 15 ॥
4.170.m: a support for living beings, with many children, dear to my husband, / longed for by the three worlds, sharing the fruits of the three goals of life?'

4.170.s:
vasiṣṭhastāmuvācātha śṛṇuṣva kathayāmi te ..
dānaṃ mānakaraṃ puṃsāṃ sarvakāmapradāyakam .. 16 ..
4.170.d:
वसिष्ठस्तामुवाचाथ शृणुष्व कथयामि ते ॥
दानं मानकरं पुंसां सर्वकामप्रदायकम् ॥ 16 ॥
4.170.m: Then Vasiṣṭha said to her: 'Listen, I will tell you / of a gift that brings honour to men and bestows all desires.

4.170.s:
kṛtvā tāmramayīṃ sthālīṃ palānāṃ pañcabhiḥ śataiḥ ..
aśaktastu tadarddhena caturthāṃśena vā punaḥ .. 17 ..
4.170.d:
कृत्वा ताम्रमयीं स्थालीं पलानां पञ्चभिः शतैः ॥
अशक्तस्तु तदर्द्धेन चतुर्थांशेन वा पुनः ॥ 17 ॥
4.170.m: Having made a copper pot of five hundred palas, / or if unable, half of that, or even a fourth part,

4.170.s:
sarvaśaktivihīnastu mṛnmayīmapi kārayet ..
sugaṃbhīrodaradarīdṛḍhadaṇḍakuṭuṃbakām .. . .. 18 ..
4.170.d:
सर्वशक्तिविहीनस्तु मृन्मयीमपि कारयेत् ॥
सुगंभीरोदरदरीदृढदण्डकुटुंबकाम् ॥ ॥। 18 ॥
4.170.m: or if completely without means, one should have even an earthenware pot made, / possessing a deep cavernous interior and a firm handle-attachment,

4.170.s:
mudgataṃdulaniṣpannasusvinnakṣiprapūritām ..
upadaṃśodakayutāṃ ghṛtapātrasamanvitām .. 19 ..
4.170.d:
मुद्गतंदुलनिष्पन्नसुस्विन्नक्षिप्रपूरिताम् ॥
उपदंशोदकयुतां घृतपात्रसमन्विताम् ॥ 19 ॥
4.170.m: filled immediately with well-cooked beans and rice, / accompanied by condiments and water, together with a bowl of ghee."

4.170.s:
dhautapārśvāṃ dhautakarṇāṃ carcitāṃ candanena ca ..
sthāpya maṃḍalake vastraiḥ puṣpadhūpairathārcayet ..4,170.20..
āditye'hani saṃkrāṃtau caturdaśyaṣṭamīṣu vā ..
ekādaśyāṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ viprāya pratipādayet .. 21 ..
4.170.d:
धौतपार्श्वां धौतकर्णां चर्चितां चन्दनेन च ॥
स्थाप्य मंडलके वस्त्रैः पुष्पधूपैरथार्चयेत् ॥4,170.20॥
आदित्येऽहनि संक्रांतौ चतुर्दश्यष्टमीषु वा ॥
एकादश्यां तृतीयायां विप्राय प्रतिपादयेत् ॥ 21 ॥
4.170.m: With its sides and rim washed, and smeared with sandalwood paste, / having placed it upon a diagram, one should then worship it with garments, flowers, and incense. / On a Sunday, at a solstice, or on the fourteenth or eighth lunar day, / on the eleventh or the third, he should present it to a brāhmaṇa.

4.170.s:
jvalajjvalanapārśvasthaistaṃḍulaiḥ sajalairapi ..
na bhavedbhojyasaṃsiddhirbhūtānāṃ piṭharīṃ vinā .. 22 ..
4.170.d:
ज्वलज्ज्वलनपार्श्वस्थैस्तंडुलैः सजलैरपि ॥
न भवेद्भोज्यसंसिद्धिर्भूतानां पिठरीं विना ॥ 22 ॥
4.170.m: Even with grains accompanied by water placed near a blazing fire, / the preparation of food for living beings cannot happen without a pot.

4.170.s:
tvaṃ siddhiḥ siddhikāmānāṃ tvaṃ puṣṭiḥ puṣṭimicchatām ..
atastvāṃ praṇamāmyāśu satyaṃ kuru vaco mama .. 23 ..
4.170.d:
त्वं सिद्धिः सिद्धिकामानां त्वं पुष्टिः पुष्टिमिच्छताम् ॥
अतस्त्वां प्रणमाम्याशु सत्यं कुरु वचो मम ॥ 23 ॥
4.170.m: You are accomplishment for those who desire accomplishment; you are nourishment for those who wish for nourishment. / Therefore I bow to you at once; make my word come true.

4.170.s:
jñātibaṃdhusuhṛdvarge vipre preṣyajane tathā ..
abhuktavati nāśnīyāttathā bhava varapradā .. ..24..
4.170.d:
ज्ञातिबंधुसुहृद्वर्गे विप्रे प्रेष्यजने तथा ॥
अभुक्तवति नाश्नीयात्तथा भव वरप्रदा ॥ ॥24॥
4.170.m: While kinsmen, relatives, friends, / the brāhmaṇa, and servants have not eaten, may I not eat; thus be the bestower of boons.

4.170.s:
ityuccārya pradātavyā haṃḍikā dvijapuṃgave ..
tuṣṭipuṣṭipradā puṃsāṃ sarvānkāmānabhīpsatā .. 25 ..
4.170.d:
इत्युच्चार्य प्रदातव्या हंडिका द्विजपुंगवे ॥
तुष्टिपुष्टिप्रदा पुंसां सर्वान्कामानभीप्सता ॥ 25 ॥
4.170.m: Uttering this, the pot should be given to an eminent twice-born / by one who desires all wishes, as it grants contentment and nourishment to men.

4.170.s:
vasiṣṭhavacanaṃ śrutvā sā cakāra tathaiva tu ..
prādātsthālīṃ brāhmaṇāya bahūnāṃ bahudakṣiṇām .. 26 ..
4.170.d:
वसिष्ठवचनं श्रुत्वा सा चकार तथैव तु ॥
प्रादात्स्थालीं ब्राह्मणाय बहूनां बहुदक्षिणाम् ॥ 26 ॥
4.170.m: Hearing Vasiṣṭha's word, she did just so: / she gave the cooking pot along with abundant sacrificial fee to a brāhmaṇa, [capable of feeding] many.

4.170.s:
sā caiṣā draupadī pārtha bhavadbhāryā'bhavatpriyā ..
tena dānaprabhāveṇa bhavitā'śūnyapāṇikā .. .. 27 ..
4.170.d:
सा चैषा द्रौपदी पार्थ भवद्भार्याऽभवत्प्रिया ॥
तेन दानप्रभावेण भविताऽशून्यपाणिका ॥ ॥ 27 ॥
4.170.m: And she was this Draupadī, O son of Pṛthā, who became your beloved wife; / through the power of that gift, her hands will never be empty.

4.170.s:
eṣā satī śacī svāhā sāvitrī bhūraruṃdhatī ..
śrīreṣā yatra vasati na kiṃcittatra durlabham .. 28 ..
4.170.d:
एषा सती शची स्वाहा सावित्री भूररुंधती ॥
श्रीरेषा यत्र वसति न किंचित्तत्र दुर्लभम् ॥ 28 ॥
4.170.m: She is Satī, Śacī, Svāhā, Sāvitrī, Earth, and Arundhatī; / she is Śrī; where she resides, nothing is hard to obtain.

4.170.s:
anayā yā bhṛtā sthālī tayā sarvamidaṃ jagat ..
bhojayiṣyasi kauṃteya kimato brāhmaṇā amī .. 29 ..
4.170.d:
अनया या भृता स्थाली तया सर्वमिदं जगत् ॥
भोजयिष्यसि कौंतेय किमतो ब्राह्मणा अमी ॥ 29 ॥
4.170.m: By the pot filled by her, all this world / you will feed, O son of Kuntī; what then of these brāhmaṇas?

4.170.s:
maitreyāttadupaśrutya tatra saṃhṛṣṭamānasaḥ ..
pūrvaṃ bhojitavānasmi bahuviprajanā vane .. 4.170.30 ..
4.170.d:
मैत्रेयात्तदुपश्रुत्य तत्र संहृष्टमानसः ॥
पूर्वं भोजितवानस्मि बहुविप्रजना वने ॥ 4.170.30 ॥
4.170.m: Having heard that from Maitreya, with a delighted mind / I previously fed many brāhmaṇas in the forest.

4.170.s:
annadānaprasaṃgena sthālīdānamidaṃ mayā ..
kathitaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa kṣaṃtavyamanasūyayā .. 31 ..
4.170.d:
अन्नदानप्रसंगेन स्थालीदानमिदं मया ॥
कथितं पुण्डरीकाक्ष क्षंतव्यमनसूयया ॥ 31 ॥
4.170.m: In connection with the gift of food, this gift of a cooking pot / has been recounted by me, O lotus-eyed one; it should be forgiven without ill will.

4.170.s:
sthālīṃ viśālavadanāṃ ca sataṃḍulāṃ ca yacchaṃti ye madhuraśulbamayīṃ dvijebhyaḥ ..
teṣāṃ suhṛtsvajanaviprajanena bhojyaṃ saṃbhujyamānamapi kṛṣṇa na yāti nāśam ..32..
dāsīdānavidhivarṇanam
4.170.d:
स्थालीं विशालवदनां च सतंडुलां च यच्छंति ये मधुरशुल्बमयीं द्विजेभ्यः ॥
तेषां सुहृत्स्वजनविप्रजनेन भोज्यं संभुज्यमानमपि कृष्ण न याति नाशम् ॥32॥
दासीदानविधिवर्णनम्
4.170.m:
Those who give to twice-borns a cooking pot with a wide mouth, containing grains of rice and made of pleasing copper, / their food, even while being consumed by friends, kin, and brāhmaṇas, O Kṛṣṇa, never suffers exhaustion.
Description of the procedure for the gift of a female servant

4.171.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
dāsīdānamahaṃ te'dya pravakṣyāmyarisūdana ..
bhaktyā snehācca bhavato yatroktaṃ kenacitkvacit .. 1 ..
4.171.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
दासीदानमहं तेऽद्य प्रवक्ष्याम्यरिसूदन ॥
भक्त्या स्नेहाच्च भवतो यत्रोक्तं केनचित्क्वचित् ॥ 1 ॥
4.171.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / I shall declare to you today the gift of a female servant, O destroyer of enemies, / out of devotion and affection for you, as it was stated by someone somewhere.

4.171.s:
caturṇāmāśramāṇāṃ hi gṛhasthaḥ śreṣṭha ucyate ..
gṛhasthācca gṛhaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ gṛhācchreṣṭhā varāḥ striyaḥ .. 2 ..
4.171.d:
चतुर्णामाश्रमाणां हि गृहस्थः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते ॥
गृहस्थाच्च गृहं श्रेष्ठं गृहाच्छ्रेष्ठा वराः स्त्रियः ॥ 2 ॥
4.171.m: Indeed, among the four stages of life, the householder is called the best; / better than the householder is the home, and better than the home are excellent women.

4.171.s:
pūrṇeṃdubiṃbavadanāḥ pīnonnatapayodharāḥ ..
tadgṛhaṃ yatra dṛśyaṃte yoṣitaḥ śīlamaṃḍanāḥ .. 3 ..
4.171.d:
पूर्णेंदुबिंबवदनाः पीनोन्नतपयोधराः ॥
तद्गृहं यत्र दृश्यंते योषितः शीलमंडनाः ॥ 3 ॥
4.171.m: With faces like the orb of the full moon, with plump, prominent breasts, / that is a home where women adorned with good conduct are seen.

4.171.s:
jāmayo yatra pūjyaṃte ramante tatra devatāḥ ..
yatraitāstu na pūjyaṃte vinaṃkṣyatyāśu tadgṛham .. 4 ..
4.171.d:
जामयो यत्र पूज्यंते रमन्ते तत्र देवताः ॥
यत्रैतास्तु न पूज्यंते विनंक्ष्यत्याशु तद्गृहम् ॥ 4 ॥
4.171.m: Where female relations are honoured, there the deities rejoice; / but where these are not honoured, that house will soon perish.

4.171.s:
jāmayo yāni gehāni śapaṃtyapratipūjitāḥ ..
tāni kṛtyāhatānīva sadyo yāṃti parābhavam .. 5 ..
4.171.d:
जामयो यानि गेहानि शपंत्यप्रतिपूजिताः ॥
तानि कृत्याहतानीव सद्यो यांति पराभवम् ॥ 5 ॥
4.171.m: The homes that female relations curse when unhonoured, / those quickly meet ruin, as though struck by sorcery.

4.171.s:
amṛtasyeva kuṇḍāni sukhānāmiva rāśayaḥ ..
rateriva nidhānāni yoṣitaḥ kena nirmitāḥ .. .. 6 ..
4.171.d:
अमृतस्येव कुण्डानि सुखानामिव राशयः ॥
रतेरिव निधानानि योषितः केन निर्मिताः ॥ ॥ 6 ॥
4.171.m: Like vessels of nectar, like heaps of pleasures, / like treasures of delight—by whom were women created?

4.171.s:
śyāmā maṃtharagāminyaḥ pīnonnatapayodharāḥ ..
mahiṣyo varanāryaśca na bhavaṃti gṛhegṛhe .. 7..
4.171.d:
श्यामा मंथरगामिन्यः पीनोन्नतपयोधराः ॥
महिष्यो वरनार्यश्च न भवंति गृहेगृहे ॥ 7॥
4.171.m: Dark maidens, slow-paced, with plump, prominent breasts, / noble women and chief queens are not found in every home.

4.171.s:
ahiraṇyamadāsīkamalpānnājyamagorasam ..
gṛhaṃ kṛpaṇavṛttīnāṃ narakasyāparo vidhiḥ .. 8 ..
4.171.d:
अहिरण्यमदासीकमल्पान्नाज्यमगोरसम् ॥
गृहं कृपणवृत्तीनां नरकस्यापरो विधिः ॥ 8 ॥
4.171.m: A house without gold, without a female servant, with scarce food, lacking ghee, without milk products, / belonging to those living miserly lives, is another form of hell.

4.171.s:
adaṇḍapāśikaṃ grāmamadāsīkaṃ ca yadgṛham ..
anājyaṃ bhojanaṃ yacca vṛthā taditi me matiḥ ..9..
4.171.d:
अदण्डपाशिकं ग्राममदासीकं च यद्गृहम् ॥
अनाज्यं भोजनं यच्च वृथा तदिति मे मतिः ॥9॥
4.171.m: A village without a police officer, a house without a female servant, / and a meal without ghee—that is in vain; such is my view.

4.171.s:
vibhavābharaṇā dāsyo yadgṛhaṃ samupāsate..
tatrāste paṃkajakarā lakṣmīḥ kṣīrodavāsinī ..4.171.10..
4.171.d:
विभवाभरणा दास्यो यद्गृहं समुपासते॥
तत्रास्ते पंकजकरा लक्ष्मीः क्षीरोदवासिनी ॥4.171.10॥
4.171.m: A house attended by female servants adorned with wealth, / there dwells Lakṣmī, holding a lotus, who resides in the milk ocean.

4.171.s:
na yatrāsti gṛhe śaucaṃ na sukhaṃ vyavahārajam..
yatra vā nāsti dāsyekā tatsadaivānavasthitam..11..
4.171.d:
न यत्रास्ति गृहे शौचं न सुखं व्यवहारजम्॥
यत्र वा नास्ति दास्येका तत्सदैवानवस्थितम्॥11॥
4.171.m: In a house where there is no purity, no pleasure born of daily affairs, / or where there is not even one female servant, that house is forever disordered.

4.171.s:
yatra karmakarī nāsti sarvakarmakarī sadā..
na tacchataṃ kiṃkarāṇāṃ karoti śubhatāmapi..12..
4.171.d:
यत्र कर्मकरी नास्ति सर्वकर्मकरी सदा॥
न तच्छतं किंकराणां करोति शुभतामपि॥12॥
4.171.m: Where there is no maidservant performing all tasks at all times, / even a hundred male servants do not bring auspiciousness to that [house].

4.171.s:
yadekā kurute dāsī gṛhasthena bhṛtā hi sā..
bahulokākulo grāmo dāsīdāsākulaṃ gṛham .. 13 ..
4.171.d:
यदेका कुरुते दासी गृहस्थेन भृता हि सा॥
बहुलोकाकुलो ग्रामो दासीदासाकुलं गृहम् ॥ 13 ॥
4.171.m: What a single female servant maintained by the householder does, [is unmatched]; / a village is crowded with many people, but a house is bustling with male and female servants.

4.171.s:
buddhirdharmākulā yasya tasya cetaḥ kimākulam ..
yatra bhāryāgṛhe dakṣā dāsyakarmaṇyanuvratāḥ ..14..
4.171.d:
बुद्धिर्धर्माकुला यस्य तस्य चेतः किमाकुलम् ॥
यत्र भार्यागृहे दक्षा दास्यकर्मण्यनुव्रताः ॥14॥
4.171.m: He whose intellect is filled with righteousness—why would his mind be distressed? / In whose home wives are capable, and female servants devoted to their duties,

4.171.s:
bhṛtyāḥ sadodyamaparāstrivargastatra dṛśyate..
yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ loke tattaddeyamiti śrutiḥ .. 15 ..
4.171.d:
भृत्याः सदोद्यमपरास्त्रिवर्गस्तत्र दृश्यते॥
यद्यदिष्टतमं लोके तत्तद्देयमिति श्रुतिः ॥ 15 ॥
4.171.m: and servants are always energetic, there the threefold aim of life is seen. / 'Whatever is dearest in the world, that very thing should be given'—so says the scripture.

4.171.s:
etadvicārya hṛdaye deyā dāsī dvijātaye ..
sthiranakṣatrasaṃyukte some saumyagrahānvite .. 1 6..
4.171.d:
एतद्विचार्य हृदये देया दासी द्विजातये ॥
स्थिरनक्षत्रसंयुक्ते सोमे सौम्यग्रहान्विते ॥ 1 6॥
4.171.m: Reflecting on this in one's heart, a female servant should be given to a twice-born, / on a Monday conjoined with a fixed lunar asterism, attended by auspicious planets.

4.171.s:
dānakālaṃ praśaṃsaṃti saṃtaḥ parvaṇi vā punaḥ ..
alaṃkṛtya yathāśaktyā vāsobhirbhūṣaṇaistathā .. 17..
4.171.d:
दानकालं प्रशंसंति संतः पर्वणि वा पुनः ॥
अलंकृत्य यथाशक्त्या वासोभिर्भूषणैस्तथा ॥ 17॥
4.171.m: The virtuous praise the time of gift-giving, or again on a sacred junction day; / having adorned her according to one's means with clothes and ornaments,

4.171.s:
brāhmaṇāya pradātavyā maṃtreṇānena kaurava ..
iyaṃ dāsī mayā tubhyaṃ bhagavanpratipāditā .. 18 ..
4.171.d:
ब्राह्मणाय प्रदातव्या मंत्रेणानेन कौरव ॥
इयं दासी मया तुभ्यं भगवन्प्रतिपादिता ॥ 18 ॥
4.171.m: she should be given to a brāhmaṇa with this mantra, O descendant of Kuru: / 'This female servant has been bestowed by me upon you, O venerable one;

4.171.s:
karmopayojyā bhojyā vā yatheṣṭaṃ bhadramastu te ..
dattvā kṣamāpayetpaścādbrāhmaṇaṃ kāṃcanena tam..19..
4.171.d:
कर्मोपयोज्या भोज्या वा यथेष्टं भद्रमस्तु ते ॥
दत्त्वा क्षमापयेत्पश्चाद्ब्राह्मणं कांचनेन तम्॥19॥
4.171.m: she may be employed for work or enjoyed as you please; may good betide you.' / Having given her, he should afterwards propitiate that brāhmaṇa with gold.

4.171.s:
anuvrajya gṛhadvāraṃ yāvatpaścādvisarjayet..
anena vidhinā dadyādaṃkayitvā surālaye..4.171.20..
4.171.d:
अनुव्रज्य गृहद्वारं यावत्पश्चाद्विसर्जयेत्॥
अनेन विधिना दद्यादंकयित्वा सुरालये॥4.171.20॥
4.171.m: Having accompanied him as far as the doorway of the house, he should then dismiss him. / According to this rule, one may give her after marking her in a temple,

4.171.s:
makhe cāpi mahārāja prasiddhe vā pratiśraye ..
sarvakarmakarī dattvā taruṇīṃ rūpaśālinīm ..21..
4.171.d:
मखे चापि महाराज प्रसिद्धे वा प्रतिश्रये ॥
सर्वकर्मकरी दत्त्वा तरुणीं रूपशालिनीम् ॥21॥
4.171.m: or at a sacrifice, O great king, or in a well-known shelter. / Having given a young, beautiful woman who does all work,

4.171.s: prāpyate yatphalaṃ puṃbhiḥ pārtha tatkena varṇyate .. 22 ..
4.171.d: प्राप्यते यत्फलं पुंभिः पार्थ तत्केन वर्ण्यते ॥ 22 ॥
4.171.m: what fruit is attained by men, O son of Pṛthā—by whom could that be described?

4.171.s:
dāsīṃ samīkṣya bahuśo gṛhakarmadakṣāṃ yo brahmaṇāya kulaśīlavate dadāti ..
vidyādharādhipaśatairapi pūjito'sau lokaṃ trilokaramayāpsarasāṃ prayāti .. 23 ..
prapādānavidhivarṇanam
4.171.d:
दासीं समीक्ष्य बहुशो गृहकर्मदक्षां यो ब्रह्मणाय कुलशीलवते ददाति ॥
विद्याधराधिपशतैरपि पूजितोऽसौ लोकं त्रिलोकरमयाप्सरसां प्रयाति ॥ 23 ॥
प्रपादानविधिवर्णनम्
4.171.m:
Having closely examined a female servant skilled in household work, he who gives her to a brāhmaṇa of noble family and good conduct, / worshipped even by hundreds of vidyādhara lords, goes to the world of apsarases that charms the three worlds.
Description of the procedure for the gift of a water booth

4.172.s:
.. yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
prapādānasya māhātmyaṃ vada devakinaṃdana ..
kathaṃ deyā kadā deyā dāne tasyāśca kiṃ phalam .. 1 ..
4.172.d:
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
प्रपादानस्य माहात्म्यं वद देवकिनंदन ॥
कथं देया कदा देया दाने तस्याश्च किं फलम् ॥ 1 ॥
4.172.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Tell of the greatness of the gift of a water booth, O son of Devakī: / How is it to be given, when is it to be given, and what is the fruit of its giving?

4.172.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
atīte phālgune māsi prāpte caitre mahotsave ..
puṇye'hni viprakathite grahacaṃdrabalānvite .. 2 ..
4.172.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
अतीते फाल्गुने मासि प्राप्ते चैत्रे महोत्सवे ॥
पुण्येऽह्नि विप्रकथिते ग्रहचंद्रबलान्विते ॥ 2 ॥
4.172.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / When the month of Phālguna has passed and the great festival of Caitra has arrived, / on an auspicious day declared by brāhmaṇas, endowed with planetary and lunar strength,

4.172.s:
maṃḍapaṃ kārayedvidvānghanacchāyaṃ manoramam ..
purasya madhye pathi vā kāṃtāre toyavarjite .. 3 ..
4.172.d:
मंडपं कारयेद्विद्वान्घनच्छायं मनोरमम् ॥
पुरस्य मध्ये पथि वा कांतारे तोयवर्जिते ॥ 3 ॥
4.172.m: a wise man should erect a pavilion offering dense shade and pleasing to the mind, / in the middle of a city, or on a road, or in a forest devoid of water,

4.172.s:
devatāyatane vāpi caityavṛkṣatale'pi vā ..
suśītalaṃ ca ramyaṃ ca vicitrāsanasaṃyutam .. 4 ..
4.172.d:
देवतायतने वापि चैत्यवृक्षतलेऽपि वा ॥
सुशीतलं च रम्यं च विचित्रासनसंयुतम् ॥ 4 ॥
4.172.m: or in a temple of the gods, or beneath a sacred fig tree— / very cool, delightful, and furnished with various seats.

4.172.s:
kārayenmaṃḍapaṃ bhavyaṃ śītavātasahaṃ dṛḍham ..
tanmadhye sthāpayedbhaktyā maṇīnkuṃbhāṃśca śobhanān .. 5 ..
4.172.d:
कारयेन्मंडपं भव्यं शीतवातसहं दृढम् ॥
तन्मध्ये स्थापयेद्भक्त्या मणीन्कुंभांश्च शोभनान् ॥ 5 ॥
4.172.m: He should have a grand pavilion made, enduring cold and wind, firmly built; / in its middle he should devotedly place jewels and beautiful water pots,

4.172.s:
akālamūlānkarakānvastrairāveṣṭitānatha ..
brāhmaṇaḥ śīlasaṃpanno vṛttiṃ dattvā yathocitām .. 6 ..
4.172.d:
अकालमूलान्करकान्वस्त्रैरावेष्टितानथ ॥
ब्राह्मणः शीलसंपन्नो वृत्तिं दत्त्वा यथोचिताम् ॥ 6 ॥
4.172.m: and small water vessels with broad bases, wrapped in cloths. / Then a virtuous brāhmaṇa, having been given a suitable livelihood,

4.172.s:
prapāpālaḥ prakartavyo bahuputraparicchadaḥ ..
pānīyapānenāśrāṃtānyaḥ kārayati mānavān ..7..
4.172.d:
प्रपापालः प्रकर्तव्यो बहुपुत्रपरिच्छदः ॥
पानीयपानेनाश्रांतान्यः कारयति मानवान् ॥7॥
4.172.m: having many sons and a household, should be appointed as the water-station keeper, / who relieves weary men by serving drinking water.

4.172.s:
evaṃvidhāṃ prapāṃ kṛtvā śubhe'hni vidhipūrvakam ..
yathāśaktyā naraśreṣṭha prāraṃbhe bhojayeddvijān .. 8 ..
4.172.d:
एवंविधां प्रपां कृत्वा शुभेऽह्नि विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
यथाशक्त्या नरश्रेष्ठ प्रारंभे भोजयेद्द्विजान् ॥ 8 ॥
4.172.m: Having arranged such a water-station on an auspicious day according to the prescribed rules, / O best of men, he should feed brāhmaṇas at the inauguration according to his means.

4.172.s:
tataścotsarjayedviprānmaṃtreṇānena mānavaḥ ..
prapeyaṃ sarvasāmānyā bhūtebhyaḥ pratipāditā .. 9 ..
4.172.d:
ततश्चोत्सर्जयेद्विप्रान्मंत्रेणानेन मानवः ॥
प्रपेयं सर्वसामान्या भूतेभ्यः प्रतिपादिता ॥ 9 ॥
4.172.m: Then the man should dismiss the brāhmaṇas with this mantra: / 'This water-station, common to all, has been provided for all beings;

4.172.s:
asyāḥ pradānātpitarastṛpyaṃtu ca pitāmahāḥ ..
anivāryaṃ tato deyaṃ jalaṃ māsacatuṣṭayam .. 4.172.10 ..
4.172.d:
अस्याः प्रदानात्पितरस्तृप्यंतु च पितामहाः ॥
अनिवार्यं ततो देयं जलं मासचतुष्टयम् ॥ 4.172.10 ॥
4.172.m: by its donation, may the fathers and grandfathers be satisfied!' / Thereafter, water should be given without hindrance for four months,

4.172.s:
tripakṣaṃ vā mahārāja jīvānāṃ jīvanaṃ param ..
gaṃdhāḍhyaṃ surasaṃ śītaṃ śobhane bhājane sthitam .. 11 ..
4.172.d:
त्रिपक्षं वा महाराज जीवानां जीवनं परम् ॥
गंधाढ्यं सुरसं शीतं शोभने भाजने स्थितम् ॥ 11 ॥
4.172.m: or for three fortnights, O great king—water, the supreme life of living beings, / richly fragrant, delicious, cold, and placed in a handsome vessel.

4.172.s:
pradadyādapratihataṃ mukhaṃ cānavalokayan ..
pratyahaṃ kārayettasyāṃ śaktito dvijabhojanam .. 12 ..
4.172.d:
प्रदद्यादप्रतिहतं मुखं चानवलोकयन् ॥
प्रत्यहं कारयेत्तस्यां शक्तितो द्विजभोजनम् ॥ 12 ॥
4.172.m: He should give it unhindered, without looking at the [recipient's] face; / and according to his means, he should feed brāhmaṇas there daily.

4.172.s:
anena vidhinā yastu grīṣmoṣmaśoṣanāśanam ..
pānīyamuttamaṃ dadyāttasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .. 13..
4.172.d:
अनेन विधिना यस्तु ग्रीष्मोष्मशोषनाशनम् ॥
पानीयमुत्तमं दद्यात्तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु ॥ 13॥
4.172.m: He who, following this procedure, gives excellent drinking water / that destroys the parching heat of the summer season—hear the fruit of his merit:

4.172.s:
sarvatīrtheṣu yatpuṇyaṃ sarvadāneṣu yatphalam ..
tatpuṇyaphalamāpnoti sarvadevaiḥ supūjitaḥ .. 14 ..
4.172.d:
सर्वतीर्थेषु यत्पुण्यं सर्वदानेषु यत्फलम् ॥
तत्पुण्यफलमाप्नोति सर्वदेवैः सुपूजितः ॥ 14 ॥
4.172.m: Whatever merit is found in all sacred places, whatever fruit exists in all gifts, / that fruit of merit he attains, highly honoured by all the gods.

4.172.s:
pūrṇacaṃdrapratīkāśaṃ vimānaṃ sodhiruhya ca ..
yāti devendranagare pūjyamāno'psarogaṇaiḥ .. 15 ..
4.172.d:
पूर्णचंद्रप्रतीकाशं विमानं सोधिरुह्य च ॥
याति देवेन्द्रनगरे पूज्यमानोऽप्सरोगणैः ॥ 15 ॥
4.172.m: And mounting a celestial chariot resembling the full moon, / he goes to the city of the lord of gods, worshipped by hosts of apsarases.

4.172.s:
viṃśatkoṭyo hi varṣāṇāṃ yakṣagandharvasevitaḥ ..
puṇyakṣayādihāgatya caturvedī dvijo bhavet .. 16 ..
4.172.d:
विंशत्कोट्यो हि वर्षाणां यक्षगन्धर्वसेवितः ॥
पुण्यक्षयादिहागत्य चतुर्वेदी द्विजो भवेत् ॥ 16 ॥
4.172.m: Attended by yakṣas and gandharvas for two hundred million years, / upon the exhaustion of his merit, he comes here and becomes a brāhmaṇa master of the four Vedas.

4.172.s:
tataḥ paraṃ padaṃ yāti punarāvṛttidurlabham ..
prapādānāsamarthena viśeṣāddharmamīpsatā .. 174
4.172.d:
ततः परं पदं याति पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभम् ॥
प्रपादानासमर्थेन विशेषाद्धर्ममीप्सता ॥ 174
4.172.m: Thereafter he goes to the supreme state, whence rebirth is hard to encounter. / By one unable to give a water-station, yet particularly desiring merit,

4.172.s:
pratyahaṃ dharmaghaṭakaḥ karpaṭāveṣṭitānanaḥ ..
brāhmaṇasya gṛhe neyaḥ śītāmalajalaḥ śuciḥ .. 18 ..
4.172.d:
प्रत्यहं धर्मघटकः कर्पटावेष्टिताननः ॥
ब्राह्मणस्य गृहे नेयः शीतामलजलः शुचिः ॥ 18 ॥
4.172.m: a water jar of righteousness, pure, containing cool and clean water, / with its mouth covered with cloth, should daily be taken to the house of a brāhmaṇa.

4.172.s:
tasyaivodyāpanaṃ kāryaṃ māsimāsi narottama ..
maṃḍakāveṣṭikābhiśca pakvānnaiḥ sārvakāmikaiḥ .. 19 ..
4.172.d:
तस्यैवोद्यापनं कार्यं मासिमासि नरोत्तम ॥
मंडकावेष्टिकाभिश्च पक्वान्नैः सार्वकामिकैः ॥ 19 ॥
4.172.m: Its concluding rite should be performed month after month, O best of men, / with puffed flatbreads, rolled dough cakes, and cooked foods fulfilling all desires.

4.172.s:
uddiśya śaṃkaraṃ viṣṇuṃ brahmāṇaṃ kurunandana ..
salilaṃ prokṣayitvā tu maṃtreṇānena mānavaḥ .. 4.172.20 ..
4.172.d:
उद्दिश्य शंकरं विष्णुं ब्रह्माणं कुरुनन्दन ॥
सलिलं प्रोक्षयित्वा तु मंत्रेणानेन मानवः ॥ 4.172.20 ॥
4.172.m: Addressing Śaṅkara, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā, O son of Kuru, / the man, having sprinkled the water, [should recite] with this mantra:

4.172.s:
eṣa dharmaghaṭo datto brahmaviṣṇuśivātmakaḥ ..
asya pradānātsaphalā mama saṃtu manorathāḥ .. 23 .. (iti dharmaghaṭadānamaṃtraḥ)
4.172.d:
एष धर्मघटो दत्तो ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवात्मकः ॥
अस्य प्रदानात्सफला मम संतु मनोरथाः ॥ 23 ॥ (इति धर्मघटदानमंत्रः)
4.172.m: 'This water jar of righteousness is given, whose nature is Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva; / by the donation of this, may my desires bear fruit.' (Thus the mantra for donating the water jar of righteousness.)

4.172.s:
anena vidhinā yastu dharmakuṃbhaṃ prayacchati ..
prapādānaphalaṃ so'pi prāpnotīha na saṃśayaḥ .. 22 ..
4.172.d:
अनेन विधिना यस्तु धर्मकुंभं प्रयच्छति ॥
प्रपादानफलं सोऽपि प्राप्नोतीह न संशयः ॥ 22 ॥
4.172.m: He who gives a water jar of righteousness according to this procedure / also attains the fruit of giving a water-station in this world; of this there is no doubt.

4.172.s:
dharmakuṃbhapradāne'pi yadyaśaktaḥ pumānbhavet ..
tenāśvatthatarormūlaṃ secyaṃ nityaṃ jitātmanā .. 23 ..
4.172.d:
धर्मकुंभप्रदानेऽपि यद्यशक्तः पुमान्भवेत् ॥
तेनाश्वत्थतरोर्मूलं सेच्यं नित्यं जितात्मना ॥ 23 ॥
4.172.m: If a man should be incapable even of the donation of a water jar of righteousness, / by him, self-controlled, the root of an aśvattha tree should daily be watered:

4.172.s:
aśvattharūpī bhagavānprīyatāṃ me janārdanaḥ ..
ityuccārya namaskṛtya pratyahaṃ pāpanāśanam ..24..
4.172.d:
अश्वत्थरूपी भगवान्प्रीयतां मे जनार्दनः ॥
इत्युच्चार्य नमस्कृत्य प्रत्यहं पापनाशनम् ॥24॥
4.172.m: 'May the Blessed Lord Janārdana in the form of an aśvattha be pleased with me.' / Having uttered this and bowed, [the watering] that destroys sin daily,

4.172.s:
yaḥ karoti tarormūle sekaṃ māsacatuṣṭayam ..
sopi tatphalamāpnoti śrutireṣā sanātanī..25..
4.172.d:
यः करोति तरोर्मूले सेकं मासचतुष्टयम् ॥
सोपि तत्फलमाप्नोति श्रुतिरेषा सनातनी॥25॥
4.172.m: whoever waters the root of the tree for four months, / he too attains that fruit; this is the eternal revelation.

4.172.s:
susvāduśītasalilā klamanāśinī ca prāṃte purasya pathi pāṃthasamājabhūmau ..
yasya prapā bhavati sarvajanopabhogyā dharmottaraḥ sa khalu jīvati jīvaloke ..26..
4.172.d:
सुस्वादुशीतसलिला क्लमनाशिनी च प्रांते पुरस्य पथि पांथसमाजभूमौ ॥
यस्य प्रपा भवति सर्वजनोपभोग्या धर्मोत्तरः स खलु जीवति जीवलोके ॥26॥
4.172.m: One whose water-station—having delicious, cool water and dispelling fatigue, / located at the edge of the town, on the road, on ground where travellers gather—is enjoyed by all people, / he lives in the world of the living, excelling in righteousness.

4.172.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇa uttaraparvaṇi śrīkṛṣṇayudhiṣṭhirasaṃvāde prapādānavidhivarṇanaṃnāma dvisaptatyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ.. ..172..
agnīṣṭikādānavidhivarṇanam
4.172.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराण उत्तरपर्वणि श्रीकृष्णयुधिष्ठिरसंवादे प्रपादानविधिवर्णनंनाम द्विसप्तत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः॥ ॥172॥
अग्नीष्टिकादानविधिवर्णनम्
4.172.m:
Thus ends the hundred and seventy-second chapter, named 'The Description of the Rite of Giving a Water-Station,' in the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira, in the Uttaraparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣyamahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Rite of Giving a Warming-Fire

4.173.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
agnīṣṭikā kathaṃ deyā śiśire śītabhīrubhiḥ ..
sarvasattvopakārāya karuṇīkṛtamānasaiḥ..1..
4.173.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
अग्नीष्टिका कथं देया शिशिरे शीतभीरुभिः ॥
सर्वसत्त्वोपकाराय करुणीकृतमानसैः॥1॥
4.173.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / How should a warming-fire be given in winter by those who fear the cold, / whose minds are softened with compassion for the benefit of all living beings?

4.173.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
agnīṣṭikāmahaṃ pārtha kathayāmi nibodha tām.
yathā yena vidhānena sarvasatvasukhapradām .. 2 ..
4.173.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
अग्नीष्टिकामहं पार्थ कथयामि निबोध ताम्।
यथा येन विधानेन सर्वसत्वसुखप्रदाम् ॥ 2 ॥
4.173.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / I will explain the warming-fire, O Pārtha; understand it: / how and by what procedure it gives comfort to all beings.

4.173.s:
ādau mārgaśire māsi śobhane divase śubhām ..
agnīṣṭikāṃ kārayitvā sukhāsanavatīṃ śubhām .. 3 ..
4.173.d:
आदौ मार्गशिरे मासि शोभने दिवसे शुभाम् ॥
अग्नीष्टिकां कारयित्वा सुखासनवतीं शुभाम् ॥ 3 ॥
4.173.m: First, in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, on an auspicious day, / having set up an auspicious warming-fire furnished with comfortable seats,

4.173.s:
devāṃgaṇe pathe gehe vistīrṇe catvaretha vā ..
ubhayoḥ saṃdhyayoḥ kṛtvā saṃśuṣkaṃ kāṣṭhasaṃcayam .. 4 ..
4.173.d:
देवांगणे पथे गेहे विस्तीर्णे चत्वरेथ वा ॥
उभयोः संध्ययोः कृत्वा संशुष्कं काष्ठसंचयम् ॥ 4 ॥
4.173.m: in a temple courtyard, on a road, in a house, or in a spacious public square, / having arranged a pile of dried wood at both twilights,

4.173.s:
tataḥ prajvālayedagniṃ hutvā vyāhṛtibhiḥ kramāt..
anena vidhinā hutvā pratyahaṃ jvālayettataḥ .. 5 ..
4.173.d:
ततः प्रज्वालयेदग्निं हुत्वा व्याहृतिभिः क्रमात्॥
अनेन विधिना हुत्वा प्रत्यहं ज्वालयेत्ततः ॥ 5 ॥
4.173.m: he should then kindle the fire, having offered oblations with the sacred utterances in order; / having offered oblations according to this rule, he should thereafter kindle it daily.

4.173.s:
yadi kaścitkṣudhārthī syādbhojyaṃ tasmai prakalpayet ..
sukhāsīno janastatra viśīto vijvarastathā .. 6 ..
4.173.d:
यदि कश्चित्क्षुधार्थी स्याद्भोज्यं तस्मै प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
सुखासीनो जनस्तत्र विशीतो विज्वरस्तथा ॥ 6 ॥
4.173.m: If anyone should be hungry, he should provide food for him; / seated comfortably there, free from cold and also free from affliction,

4.173.s:
yaḥ karoti kathāḥ pārtha na tāḥ śakyā mayoditum ..
rājavārtā janavārtā yadi kaścinnijecchayā .. 7 ..
4.173.d:
यः करोति कथाः पार्थ न ताः शक्या मयोदितुम् ॥
राजवार्ता जनवार्ता यदि कश्चिन्निजेच्छया ॥ 7 ॥
4.173.m: the stories that people tell, O Pārtha, cannot be recounted by me. / News of kings, news of the people—if anyone speaks of it according to his own desire,

4.173.s:
vadellokaḥ sukhāsīno na kenāpi nivāryate ..
anena vidhinā yastu dadyādagnīṣṭikāṃ naraḥ .. 8 ..
4.173.d:
वदेल्लोकः सुखासीनो न केनापि निवार्यते ॥
अनेन विधिना यस्तु दद्यादग्नीष्टिकां नरः ॥ 8 ॥
4.173.m: the people, seated comfortably, are not restrained by anyone. / The man who gives a warming-fire according to this procedure—

4.173.s:
tasya puṇyaphalaṃ rāja nkathyamānaṃ nibodha me ..
vimāne cārkasaṃkāśe samārūḍho mahādhane .. 9 ..
4.173.d:
तस्य पुण्यफलं राज न्कथ्यमानं निबोध मे ॥
विमाने चार्कसंकाशे समारूढो महाधने ॥ 9 ॥
4.173.m: hear from me the fruit of his merit as it is told, O king: / having mounted a costly celestial chariot resembling the sun,

4.173.s:
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭivarṣaśatāni ca ..
harṣito'tyaṃtasukhito brahmaloke mahīyate .. 4.173.10 ..
4.173.d:
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि षष्टिवर्षशतानि च ॥
हर्षितोऽत्यंतसुखितो ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ 4.173.10 ॥
4.173.m: for sixty thousand and sixty hundred years, / delighted and exceedingly happy, he is magnified in the world of Brahmā.

4.173.s:
iha lokevatīrṇaśca caturvedo dvijo bhavet ..
nīrujaḥ satrayājī ca agnivattejasānvitaḥ .. 11 ..
4.173.d:
इह लोकेवतीर्णश्च चतुर्वेदो द्विजो भवेत् ॥
नीरुजः सत्रयाजी च अग्निवत्तेजसान्वितः ॥ 11 ॥
4.173.m: And descended into this world, he becomes a brāhmaṇa knowing the four Vedas, / free from disease, a sacrificer in communal soma rites, endowed with splendour like fire.

4.173.s:
caitye surāṃgaṇasabhāvasathe subhavyāṃ ye'gnīṣṭikāṃ pracurakāṣṭhavatīṃ pradadyuḥ ..
hemaṃtaśaiśiraṛtau sukhadā janānāṃ kāyāgnidīpanamalaṃ punarāpnuvaṃti .. 12 .. ..
vidyādānavidhivarṇanam
4.173.d:
चैत्ये सुरांगणसभावसथे सुभव्यां येऽग्नीष्टिकां प्रचुरकाष्ठवतीं प्रदद्युः ॥
हेमंतशैशिरऋतौ सुखदा जनानां कायाग्निदीपनमलं पुनराप्नुवंति ॥ 12 ॥ ॥
विद्यादानविधिवर्णनम्
4.173.m:
Those who provide a grand warming-fire with abundant firewood / at a caitya, a temple courtyard, a hall, or an inn, giving comfort to people in the cold and winter seasons, / fully obtain the kindling of their bodily fire.
Description of the Rite of Giving Knowledge

4.174.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
bahupradānaṃ godānaṃ tvatto vidvañchrutaṃ mayā ..
bhūmidānasya māhātmyaṃ vidhiścaivāvadhāritaḥ .. 1 ..
4.174.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
बहुप्रदानं गोदानं त्वत्तो विद्वञ्छ्रुतं मया ॥
भूमिदानस्य माहात्म्यं विधिश्चैवावधारितः ॥ 1 ॥
4.174.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / The abundant gift, the gift of a cow, has been heard by me from you, O wise one; / and the greatness and procedure of the gift of land have been understood.

4.174.s:
sāṃprataṃ yaduśārdūla vidyādānasya yo vidhiḥ ..
tamahaṃ śrotumicchāmi kathayasva janārdana .. 2 ..
4.174.d:
सांप्रतं यदुशार्दूल विद्यादानस्य यो विधिः ॥
तमहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि कथयस्व जनार्दन ॥ 2 ॥
4.174.m: Now, O tiger of the Yadus, the procedure for the gift of knowledge: / that I wish to hear; relate it, O Janārdana!

4.174.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
vidyādānavidhiṃ vakṣye yāthātathyena te'dhunā ..
yathā deyaṃ phalaṃ yacca dattena kurunaṃdana .. 3 ..
4.174.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
विद्यादानविधिं वक्ष्ये याथातथ्येन तेऽधुना ॥
यथा देयं फलं यच्च दत्तेन कुरुनंदन ॥ 3 ॥
4.174.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / I will now declare to you truthfully the procedure for the gift of knowledge: / how it should be given, and what fruit comes when it is given, O son of Kuru.

4.174.s:
śubhe'hni viprakathite gomayena suśobhanam ..
kārayenmaṃḍalaṃ divyaṃ caturasraṃ samaṃtataḥ .. 4 ..
4.174.d:
शुभेऽह्नि विप्रकथिते गोमयेन सुशोभनम् ॥
कारयेन्मंडलं दिव्यं चतुरस्रं समंततः ॥ 4 ॥
4.174.m: On an auspicious day declared by a brāhmaṇa, with cow dung, / he should have a lovely, divine diagram made that is square on all sides,

4.174.s:
puṣpaprakarasaṃchannaṃ svastikādi vibhūṣitam..
pustakaṃ tatra saṃsthāpya gaṃdhapuṣpaiḥ samarcayet .. 5 ..
4.174.d:
पुष्पप्रकरसंछन्नं स्वस्तिकादि विभूषितम्॥
पुस्तकं तत्र संस्थाप्य गंधपुष्पैः समर्चयेत् ॥ 5 ॥
4.174.m: strewn with scattered flowers, adorned with svastikas and the like; / having placed the book there, he should worship it with fragrances and flowers.

4.174.s:
sauvarṇīṃ lekhanī kāryā raupyaṃ ca maṣibhājanam ..
lekhakaṃ pūjayitvā tu āraṃbhaṃ kārayetsudhīḥ .. 6 ..
4.174.d:
सौवर्णीं लेखनी कार्या रौप्यं च मषिभाजनम् ॥
लेखकं पूजयित्वा तु आरंभं कारयेत्सुधीः ॥ 6 ॥
4.174.m: A golden pen should be made, and an inkpot of silver; / having honoured the scribe, the wise man should cause him to begin.

4.174.s:
vinītaścāpramattaśca tataḥ prabhṛti lekhakaḥ ..
mātrānusvārasaṃyuktaṃ padacchedasamanvitam .. 7 ..
4.174.d:
विनीतश्चाप्रमत्तश्च ततः प्रभृति लेखकः ॥
मात्रानुस्वारसंयुक्तं पदच्छेदसमन्वितम् ॥ 7 ॥
4.174.m: From that moment on, the humble and attentive scribe, / [writing] furnished with vocalic signs and anusvāras, provided with word divisions,

4.174.s:
samāni samaśīrṣāṇi vartulāni dhanāni ca ..
lekhayedakṣarāṇīha tadgatenāṃtarātmanā .. 8 ..
4.174.d:
समानि समशीर्षाणि वर्तुलानि धनानि च ॥
लेखयेदक्षराणीह तद्गतेनांतरात्मना ॥ 8 ॥
4.174.m: even, with uniform top-strokes, rounded, and solid, / should have the letters written here, with his inner self fixed upon that [text].

4.174.s:
niṣpādayitvā tacchāstraṃ śaivaṃ vāpyatha vaiṣṇavam ..
niṣpādite tataḥ pūjyo lekhako vastrabhūṣaṇaiḥ .. 9 ..
4.174.d:
निष्पादयित्वा तच्छास्त्रं शैवं वाप्यथ वैष्णवम् ॥
निष्पादिते ततः पूज्यो लेखको वस्त्रभूषणैः ॥ 9 ॥
4.174.m: Having completed that scripture, whether Śaiva or Vaiṣṇava, / when it is completed, the scribe should then be honoured with garments and ornaments.

4.174.s:
saṃpūjayitvā tacchāstraṃ deyaṃ guṇavate tadā ..
śāstrasadbhāvaviduṣe vācake ca priyaṃvade .. 4.174.10 ..
4.174.d:
संपूजयित्वा तच्छास्त्रं देयं गुणवते तदा ॥
शास्त्रसद्भावविदुषे वाचके च प्रियंवदे ॥ 4.174.10 ॥
4.174.m: Having worshipped that scripture, it should then be given to a virtuous man, / to a reciter who knows the true meaning of the scripture and speaks kindly.

4.174.s:
vastrayugmena saṃvītaṃ pustakaṃ pratipādayet ..
sāmānyaṃ sarvalokānāṃ sthāpayedatha vā maṭhe .. 11 ..
4.174.d:
वस्त्रयुग्मेन संवीतं पुस्तकं प्रतिपादयेत् ॥
सामान्यं सर्वलोकानां स्थापयेदथ वा मठे ॥ 11 ॥
4.174.m: He should present the manuscript wrapped in a pair of cloths, / or deposit it in a monastery for the common use of all people.

4.174.s:
anena vidhinā dattvā yatphalaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ ..
tadahaṃ te pravakṣyāmi yudhiṣṭhira nibodha tat .. 12 ..
4.174.d:
अनेन विधिना दत्त्वा यत्फलं प्राप्नुयान्नरः ॥
तदहं ते प्रवक्ष्यामि युधिष्ठिर निबोध तत् ॥ 12 ॥
4.174.m: What fruit a man obtains by giving in accordance with this rule, / that I shall declare to you, O Yudhiṣṭhira; listen to that!

4.174.s:
yatpuṇyaṃ tīrthayātrāyāṃ yatpuṇyaṃ yajvanāṃ tathā ..
tatpuṇyaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ vidyādānāllabhennaraḥ .. 13 ..
4.174.d:
यत्पुण्यं तीर्थयात्रायां यत्पुण्यं यज्वनां तथा ॥
तत्पुण्यं कोटिगुणितं विद्यादानाल्लभेन्नरः ॥ 13 ॥
4.174.m: Whatever merit there is in pilgrimage, whatever merit likewise belongs to sacrificers, / that merit multiplied ten million times a man obtains through the gift of knowledge.

4.174.s:
kapilānāṃ sahasreṇa samyagdattena yatphalam ..
tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti pustakasya pradāyakaḥ .. 14 ..
4.174.d:
कपिलानां सहस्रेण सम्यग्दत्तेन यत्फलम् ॥
तत्फलं समवाप्नोति पुस्तकस्य प्रदायकः ॥ 14 ॥
4.174.m: Whatever fruit [is obtained] by a thousand kapilā cows duly given, / that fruit the giver of a manuscript fully attains.

4.174.s:
purāṇaṃ bhārataṃ vāpi rāmāyaṇamathāpi vā ..
dattvā yatphalamāpnoti pārtha tatkena varṇyate .. 15 ..
4.174.d:
पुराणं भारतं वापि रामायणमथापि वा ॥
दत्त्वा यत्फलमाप्नोति पार्थ तत्केन वर्ण्यते ॥ 15 ॥
4.174.m: Having given a Purāṇa, or the Mahābhārata, or the Rāmāyaṇa, / whatever fruit one attains, O son of Pṛthā, by whom can that be described?

4.174.s:
prātarutthāya yaḥ śiṣyānadhyāpayati yatnataḥ ..
vedaśāstraṃ nṛtyagītaṃ kastena sadṛśaḥ kṛtī .. 16 ..
4.174.d:
प्रातरुत्थाय यः शिष्यानध्यापयति यत्नतः ॥
वेदशास्त्रं नृत्यगीतं कस्तेन सदृशः कृती ॥ 16 ॥
4.174.m: He who, having risen in the morning, diligently teaches his disciples / the Veda, the scriptures, or dance and song—who is accomplished like him?

4.174.s:
upādhyāyasya yo vṛttiṃ dattvā'dhyāpayate janaḥ ..
kiṃ na dattaṃ bhavettena dharmakāmārthadarśinā .. 17 ..
4.174.d:
उपाध्यायस्य यो वृत्तिं दत्त्वाऽध्यापयते जनः ॥
किं न दत्तं भवेत्तेन धर्मकामार्थदर्शिना ॥ 17 ॥
4.174.m: A person who, having provided a livelihood for a teacher, causes him to teach— / what has not been given by him, who perceives dharma, desire, and worldly wealth?

4.174.s:
chātrāṇāṃ bhojanābhyaṃgaṃ vastraṃ bhikṣāmathāpi vā ..
dattvā prāpnoti puruṣaḥ sarvakāmānna saṃśayaḥ .. 18 ..
4.174.d:
छात्राणां भोजनाभ्यंगं वस्त्रं भिक्षामथापि वा ॥
दत्त्वा प्राप्नोति पुरुषः सर्वकामान्न संशयः ॥ 18 ॥
4.174.m: Having given to students food, oil for anointing, clothing, or alms, / a man attains all his desires; there is no doubt.

4.174.s:
viveko jīvitaṃ dīrghaṃ dharmakāmārthasaṃpadaḥ ..
sarvaṃ tena bhaveddattaṃ chātrāṇāṃ poṣaṇe kṛte .. 19 ..
4.174.d:
विवेको जीवितं दीर्घं धर्मकामार्थसंपदः ॥
सर्वं तेन भवेद्दत्तं छात्राणां पोषणे कृते ॥ 19 ॥
4.174.m: Discernment, long life, and the treasures of dharma, desire, and worldly wealth— / everything is given by him when the maintenance of students is provided.

4.174.s:
śāstraṃ śastrakalāśilpaṃ yo yadicchedupārjitum ..
tasyopakārakaraṇe pārtha kāryaṃ sadā manaḥ .. 4.174.20 ..
4.174.d:
शास्त्रं शस्त्रकलाशिल्पं यो यदिच्छेदुपार्जितुम् ॥
तस्योपकारकरणे पार्थ कार्यं सदा मनः ॥ 4.174.20 ॥
4.174.m: Scripture, weaponry, arts, and crafts—whatever anyone wishes to acquire, / in rendering assistance to him, O son of Pṛthā, the mind should always be applied.

4.174.s:
vājapeyasahasrasya samyagiṣṭasya yatphalam ..
tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti vidyādānānna saṃśayaḥ .. 21 ..
4.174.d:
वाजपेयसहस्रस्य सम्यगिष्टस्य यत्फलम् ॥
तत्फलं समवाप्नोति विद्यादानान्न संशयः ॥ 21 ॥
4.174.m: Whatever fruit belongs to a thousand Vājapeya sacrifices duly performed, / that fruit one fully attains through the gift of knowledge; there is no doubt.

4.174.s:
śivālaye viṣṇugṛhe sūryasya bhavane'tha vā ..
yaḥ kārayati dharmātmā sadā pustakavācanam .. 22 ..
4.174.d:
शिवालये विष्णुगृहे सूर्यस्य भवनेऽथ वा ॥
यः कारयति धर्मात्मा सदा पुस्तकवाचनम् ॥ 22 ॥
4.174.m: In a temple of Śiva, in a house of Viṣṇu, or in an abode of Sūrya, / the righteous person who constantly arranges for the recitation of a manuscript—

4.174.s:
gobhūhiraṇyavāsāṃsi śayanānyāsanāni ca ..
pratyahaṃ tena dattāni bhavaṃti bharatarṣabha .. 23 ..
4.174.d:
गोभूहिरण्यवासांसि शयनान्यासनानि च ॥
प्रत्यहं तेन दत्तानि भवंति भरतर्षभ ॥ 23 ॥
4.174.m: cows, land, gold, garments, beds, and seats / are given by him every day, O bull of the Bharatas!

4.174.s:
dharmādharmaṃ na jānāti vidyayā rahitaḥ pumān ..
tasmātsadaiva dharmātmā vidyādānarato bhavet .. 24 ..
4.174.d:
धर्माधर्मं न जानाति विद्यया रहितः पुमान् ॥
तस्मात्सदैव धर्मात्मा विद्यादानरतो भवेत् ॥ 24 ॥
4.174.m: Devoid of knowledge, a man does not know right from wrong; / therefore, a righteous man should always be devoted to the gift of knowledge.

4.174.s:
trailokyaṃ caturo varṇāścatvāraścāśramāḥ pṛthak ..
brahmādyā devatāḥ sarvā vidyādāne pratiṣṭhitāḥ .. 25 ..
4.174.d:
त्रैलोक्यं चतुरो वर्णाश्चत्वारश्चाश्रमाः पृथक् ॥
ब्रह्माद्या देवताः सर्वा विद्यादाने प्रतिष्ठिताः ॥ 25 ॥
4.174.m: The three worlds, the four social classes, and the four distinct stages of life, / [and] all the deities headed by Brahmā, are established upon the gift of knowledge.

4.174.s:
caturyugāni rājeṃdra ekasaptatisaṃkhyayā ..
kalpaṃ viṣṇupure tiṣṭhetpūjyamānaḥ surottamaiḥ .. 26 ..
4.174.d:
चतुर्युगानि राजेंद्र एकसप्ततिसंख्यया ॥
कल्पं विष्णुपुरे तिष्ठेत्पूज्यमानः सुरोत्तमैः ॥ 26 ॥
4.174.m: For seventy-one four-age cycles, O king of kings, / [even] for an aeon, he will reside in the city of Viṣṇu, worshipped by the foremost of the gods.

4.174.s:
kṣitiṃ vopetya kālāṃte rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ ..
hastyaśvarathadānāḍhyo dātā bhoktā vimatsarī .. 27 ..
4.174.d:
क्षितिं वोपेत्य कालांते राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥
हस्त्यश्वरथदानाढ्यो दाता भोक्ता विमत्सरी ॥ 27 ॥
4.174.m: Or having returned to earth at the end of time, he becomes a righteous king, / rich in gifts of elephants, horses, and chariots, a generous giver, an enjoyer, free from envy,

4.174.s:
rūpasaubhāgyasaṃpanno dīrghāyurnīrujo bhavet ..
putraiḥ pautre parivṛto jīvecca śaradāṃ śatam .. 28 ..
4.174.d:
रूपसौभाग्यसंपन्नो दीर्घायुर्नीरुजो भवेत् ॥
पुत्रैः पौत्रे परिवृतो जीवेच्च शरदां शतम् ॥ 28 ॥
4.174.m: endowed with beauty and good fortune, long-lived, and free from disease; / surrounded by sons and grandsons, he would live for a hundred autumns.

4.174.s:
dānaṃ viśeṣaphaladaṃ jagatīha nānyādvidyāṃ vihāya vadanābjakṛtādhivāsām ..
gobhūhiraṇyagajavājirathādisarvaṃ tāṃ yacchatāṃ kimiha pārtha bhavenna dattam .. 29 .. ..
tulāpuruṣadānavidhivarṇanam
4.174.d:
दानं विशेषफलदं जगतीह नान्याद्विद्यां विहाय वदनाब्जकृताधिवासाम् ॥
गोभूहिरण्यगजवाजिरथादिसर्वं तां यच्छतां किमिह पार्थ भवेन्न दत्तम् ॥ 29 ॥ ॥
तुलापुरुषदानविधिवर्णनम्
4.174.m:
There is no other gift in this world that yields such special fruit, setting aside knowledge, which makes its abode in the lotus of the mouth; / for those who give it, what in this world could fail to be given—cows, land, gold, elephants, horses, chariots, and everything else, O son of Pṛthā?
Description of the rule for the gift of a man weighed against gold

4.175.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
purā priyavrato rājā putraḥ svāyaṃbhuvasya tu ..
pālayāmāsa vasudhāṃ prajāpatirivāparaḥ .. 1 ..
4.175.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
पुरा प्रियव्रतो राजा पुत्रः स्वायंभुवस्य तु ॥
पालयामास वसुधां प्रजापतिरिवापरः ॥ 1 ॥
4.175.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / In ancient times King Priyavrata, the son of Svāyambhuva, / protected the earth like another Prajāpati.

4.175.s:
triṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇi pālayitvā mahīmimām ..
saptadvīpānvibhajyāsau putrebhyaḥ pradadau vibhuḥ .. 2 ..
4.175.d:
त्रिंशद्वर्षसहस्राणि पालयित्वा महीमिमाम् ॥
सप्तद्वीपान्विभज्यासौ पुत्रेभ्यः प्रददौ विभुः ॥ 2 ॥
4.175.m: Having protected this earth for thirty thousand years, / that lord, dividing the seven continents, gave them to his sons.

4.175.s:
rājye nikṣipya tanayānsaptadvīpeṣu sapta saḥ ..
viṣayānupasaṃhṛtya jagāma tapase vanam .. 3 ..
4.175.d:
राज्ये निक्षिप्य तनयान्सप्तद्वीपेषु सप्त सः ॥
विषयानुपसंहृत्य जगाम तपसे वनम् ॥ 3 ॥
4.175.m: Having installed his seven sons in kingship over the seven continents, / having withdrawn from sense-objects, he went to the forest for ascetic penance.

4.175.s:
tapovanagataṃ śrutvā rājānaṃ paramadyutim ..
samājagmurmahātmāna ṛṣayastaṃ didṛkṣavaḥ .. 4 ..
4.175.d:
तपोवनगतं श्रुत्वा राजानं परमद्युतिम् ॥
समाजग्मुर्महात्मान ऋषयस्तं दिदृक्षवः ॥ 4 ॥
4.175.m: Hearing that the king of supreme splendour had gone to the penance grove, / the great-souled sages, wishing to see him, assembled there.

4.175.s:
tānāgatānṛṣīndṛṣṭvā taponirdhūtakalmaṣān ..
pūjayāmāsa medhāvī vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā .. 5 ..
4.175.d:
तानागतानृषीन्दृष्ट्वा तपोनिर्धूतकल्मषान् ॥
पूजयामास मेधावी विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा ॥ 5 ॥
4.175.m: Seeing those sages arrived, whose sins had been shaken off by penance, / the wise [king] honoured them with rites prescribed by rule,

4.175.s:
pādyārghyācamanīyena priyapraśnottareṇa ca ..
atha teṣūpaviṣṭeṣu brāhmaṇeṣu mahātmasu .. 6 ..
4.175.d:
पाद्यार्घ्याचमनीयेन प्रियप्रश्नोत्तरेण च ॥
अथ तेषूपविष्टेषु ब्राह्मणेषु महात्मसु ॥ 6 ॥
4.175.m: with water for the feet, respectful offering, water for sipping, and inquiries about their welfare and the replies thereto. / Then, when those great-souled brahmins were seated,

4.175.s:
ājagāma mahātejāḥ pulastyo brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ ..
dīpyamāno mahātejā dvitīya iva bhāskaraḥ(pāvakaḥ) .. 7 ..
4.175.d:
आजगाम महातेजाः पुलस्त्यो ब्रह्मणः सुतः ॥
दीप्यमानो महातेजा द्वितीय इव भास्करः(पावकः) ॥ 7 ॥
4.175.m: there arrived the son of Brahmā, Pulastya, of great majesty, / blazing with great radiance like a second sun.

4.175.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā munayaḥ sarve sa ca rājā mahārathaḥ ..
uttasthurvismitāḥ sarve protphullana yanāstataḥ .. 8 ..
4.175.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा मुनयः सर्वे स च राजा महारथः ॥
उत्तस्थुर्विस्मिताः सर्वे प्रोत्फुल्लन यनास्ततः ॥ 8 ॥
4.175.m: Seeing him, all the sages and that king, a great car-warrior, / all stood up in wonder, their eyes wide open with delight.

4.175.s:
kṛtvā tu saṃvidaṃ tena yathāyogyaṃ vidhānataḥ ..
viṣṭaraṃ ca dadustasmai pādyārghyācamanādikam .. 9 ..
4.175.d:
कृत्वा तु संविदं तेन यथायोग्यं विधानतः ॥
विष्टरं च ददुस्तस्मै पाद्यार्घ्याचमनादिकम् ॥ 9 ॥
4.175.m: Having exchanged greetings with him properly according to rule, / they offered him a seat, water for the feet, respectful offering, water for sipping, and so forth.

4.175.s:
tatastu munayaḥ sarve samā sīnā yathāsukham ..
cakruḥ kathā mudāyuktā vedoktavividhāśrayāḥ .. 10 ..
4.175.d:
ततस्तु मुनयः सर्वे समा सीना यथासुखम् ॥
चक्रुः कथा मुदायुक्ता वेदोक्तविविधाश्रयाः ॥ 10 ॥
4.175.m: Then all the sages, seated at ease, / engaged with joy in various discourses based upon the Veda.

4.175.s:
tataḥ kathāṃte kasmiṃścinmunayaste sarājakāḥ ..
papracchurbrahmatanayaṃ lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā .. 11 ..
4.175.d:
ततः कथांते कस्मिंश्चिन्मुनयस्ते सराजकाः ॥
पप्रच्छुर्ब्रह्मतनयं लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥ 11 ॥
4.175.m: Then, at the conclusion of a certain discourse, those sages, together with the king, / questioned the son of Brahmā, out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds:

4.175.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
bhagavankena dānena vratena niyamena vā ..
prāpyate sadgatiḥ puṃbhiḥ strībhiśca munisattama .. 12 ..
4.175.d:
॥ ऋषय ऊचुः ॥ ॥
भगवन्केन दानेन व्रतेन नियमेन वा ॥
प्राप्यते सद्गतिः पुंभिः स्त्रीभिश्च मुनिसत्तम ॥ 12 ॥
4.175.m: The sages said: / O venerable one, by what gift, votive observance, or religious restriction / is a good state attained by men and women, O best of sages?

4.175.s:
icchāmaḥ śrotumetatte rājā cāyaṃ yatavrataḥ ..
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
śṛṇudhvaṃ munayaḥ sarve rahasyaṃ pāpanārānam .. 13 ..
4.175.d:
इच्छामः श्रोतुमेतत्ते राजा चायं यतव्रतः ॥
॥ पुलस्त्य उवाच ॥ ॥
शृणुध्वं मुनयः सर्वे रहस्यं पापनारानम् ॥ 13 ॥
4.175.m: We wish to hear this from you, as does this king of restrained vows. / Pulastya said: / Listen, all you sages, to the secret that destroys sin!

4.175.s:
uttamaṃ sarva dānānāṃ samavāyaṃ vadāmi vaḥ ..
yaddattvā brahmahā goghnaḥ pitṛghno gurutalpagaḥ .. 14 ..
4.175.d:
उत्तमं सर्व दानानां समवायं वदामि वः ॥
यद्दत्त्वा ब्रह्महा गोघ्नः पितृघ्नो गुरुतल्पगः ॥ 14 ॥
4.175.m: I shall declare to you the highest combination of all gifts, / by giving which the killer of a brahmin, the killer of a cow, the killer of a father, one who violates the teacher's bed,

4.175.s:
kṛtaghnaḥ kūṭasākṣī ca mucyate pātakānnaraḥ ..
sadyo divya tanuścaiva jāyate strī tathaiva ca .. 15 ..
4.175.d:
कृतघ्नः कूटसाक्षी च मुच्यते पातकान्नरः ॥
सद्यो दिव्य तनुश्चैव जायते स्त्री तथैव च ॥ 15 ॥
4.175.m: an ungrateful person, and a false witness—a man is freed from sin, / and at once becomes possessed of a celestial body, and likewise a woman too.

4.175.s:
kṛcchracāṃdrāyaṇādyaiśca tulāpuruṣasaṃjñitaiḥ ..
vrataiśca pācayeddehamākāṃkṣanbrahmaṇaḥ padam .. 16 ..
4.175.d:
कृच्छ्रचांद्रायणाद्यैश्च तुलापुरुषसंज्ञितैः ॥
व्रतैश्च पाचयेद्देहमाकांक्षन्ब्रह्मणः पदम् ॥ 16 ॥
4.175.m: By Kṛcchra, Cāndrāyaṇa, and the like, and by votive observances / called tulāpuruṣa, one desiring the realm of Brahmā should purify the body.

4.175.s:
kṛcchracāṃdrāyaṇādīni vratāni munisattamāḥ ..
brāhmaṇānāṃ vanasthānāṃ bhikṣo raṃḍājanasya ca .. 17 ..
4.175.d:
कृच्छ्रचांद्रायणादीनि व्रतानि मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
ब्राह्मणानां वनस्थानां भिक्षो रंडाजनस्य च ॥ 17 ॥
4.175.m: Votive observances such as Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa, O best of sages, / are for brahmins, forest-dwellers, mendicants, and widows.

4.175.s:
kāyakleśena sidhyaṃti gṛhastheṣu na tāni vai ..
mahādhanāśca ye lokā rājāno ratnabhāginaḥ .. 18 ..
4.175.d:
कायक्लेशेन सिध्यंति गृहस्थेषु न तानि वै ॥
महाधनाश्च ये लोका राजानो रत्नभागिनः ॥ 18 ॥
4.175.m:
They are accomplished through bodily mortification, not indeed for householders.
And as for people who possess great wealth, kings who enjoy gems,

4.175.s:
na teṣāṃ kṛcchrasādhyo'pi kvaciddharmaḥ praśasyate ..
yadetaddraviṇaṃ nāma prāṇāścaite bahiścarāḥ .. 19 ..
4.175.d:
न तेषां कृच्छ्रसाध्योऽपि क्वचिद्धर्मः प्रशस्यते ॥
यदेतद्द्रविणं नाम प्राणाश्चैते बहिश्चराः ॥ 19 ॥
4.175.m:
for them a duty to be accomplished through severe penance is not praised anywhere.
What is called wealth is the external vital breath.

4.175.s:
tasmādbahiścaraiḥ prāṇairātmā yojyaḥ sadā budhaiḥ ..
dravyāṇāmuttamaṃ loke kāṃcanaṃ sārvakāmikam .. 20 ..
4.175.d:
तस्माद्बहिश्चरैः प्राणैरात्मा योज्यः सदा बुधैः ॥
द्रव्याणामुत्तमं लोके कांचनं सार्वकामिकम् ॥ 20 ॥
4.175.m:
Therefore, by means of external vital breath, the self should ever be engaged by the wise.
Among possessions, gold is the highest in the world, granting all desires,

4.175.s:
apatyaṃ suramukhyasya jyeṣṭhaṃ caivaṃ vibhāvasoḥ ..
tena sārddhaṃ ya ātmānaṃ tolayetprayato budhaiḥ .. 21 ..
4.175.d:
अपत्यं सुरमुख्यस्य ज्येष्ठं चैवं विभावसोः ॥
तेन सार्द्धं य आत्मानं तोलयेत्प्रयतो बुधैः ॥ 21 ॥
4.175.m:
and likewise the firstborn offspring of the chief among the gods, of Fire.
He who, disciplined with the help of wise men, should weigh himself against that,

4.175.s:
vidhūya sarvapāpāni sadyo divyatanurbhavet ..
etatpulastyamuninā ṛṣīṇāṃ pārthivasva ca .. 22 ..
4.175.d:
विधूय सर्वपापानि सद्यो दिव्यतनुर्भवेत् ॥
एतत्पुलस्त्यमुनिना ऋषीणां पार्थिवस्व च ॥ 22 ॥
4.175.m:
having shaken off all sins, will immediately obtain a celestial body.
This was related by the sage Pulastya to the sages and to the king,

4.175.s:
samākhyātaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha tebhyaśca tanmayā śrutam ..
.. yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
tulāpuruṣadānasya vidhānaṃ parameśvara .. 23 ..
4.175.d:
समाख्यातं नृपश्रेष्ठ तेभ्यश्च तन्मया श्रुतम् ॥
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
तुलापुरुषदानस्य विधानं परमेश्वर ॥ 23 ॥
4.175.m:
O best of kings, and it was heard by me from them.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
O supreme lord, the procedure for the gift of the man-balance,

4.175.s:
kathayasva mahābhāga mama bhaktānukaṃpayā ..
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājanvidhānaṃ gadato mama .. 24 ..
4.175.d:
कथयस्व महाभाग मम भक्तानुकंपया ॥
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
शृणुष्वावहितो राजन्विधानं गदतो मम ॥ 24 ॥
4.175.m:
declare [it], O fortunate one, out of compassion for me, your devotee.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen attentively, O king, as I speak the procedure,

4.175.s:
tulāpuruṣasaṃjñasya dānasyeha nṛpottama ..
vyatīpāte'yane caiva kārtikyāṃ viṣuve tathā .. 25 ..
4.175.d:
तुलापुरुषसंज्ञस्य दानस्येह नृपोत्तम ॥
व्यतीपातेऽयने चैव कार्तिक्यां विषुवे तथा ॥ 25 ॥
4.175.m:
O best of kings, of the gift known as the man-balance in this world.
